document.tekst_begin: Aan de Staatssecretaris van Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur TER BESLISSING Beslisnota Kamerbrief Dolfinarium Pagina 1 van 2 Directoraat-generaal Agro Directie Dierlijke Agroketens en Dierenwelzijn Auteur TER BESLISSING Datum aangemaakt 9 oktober 2026 Kenmerk DGA-DAD / 108614829 Kopie aan Bijlage(n) Parafenroute Aanleiding In bijgevoegde brief wordt de Tweede Kamer geïnformeerd over uw voornemen om het houden van dolfijnen in Nederland uit te faseren. Geadviseerd besluit U wordt geadviseerd akkoord te gaan met het verzenden van deze brief aan de Tweede Kamer. Kernpunten • Gezien de zorgen die leven over het welzijn van dolfijnen in gevangenschap, zijn drie opties om het houden van dolfijnen in Nederland uit te faseren verkend en aan u voorgelegd: 1. Het faciliteren van een maatschappelijke dialoog om een definitief einde te maken aan het fokken met dolfijnen in Nederland. 2. Het opleggen van een fokverbod aan het Dolfinarium via vergunningsvoorschriften. 3. Het instellen van een houdverbod met een overgangstermijn voor de dieren die nu al in Nederland leven. Deze dieren kunnen blijven totdat zij overlijden, maar er mogen geen nieuwe dieren worden gefokt of geïmportee

Maar dit bestemmingsplan bevat dus nog een aantal gebreken en is daarmee nog niet definitief.

Boom van het jaar is rode beuk in Middelstum
items.samenvatting_bron: De rode beuk bij de ingang van de Sint-Hippolytuskerk in Middelstum (Groningen) heeft de publieksverkiezing voor Boom van het Jaar gewonnen. De boom van ruim 150 jaar oud kreeg bijna 3000 stemmen meer dan de nummer twee, die in Utrecht staat. De verkiezing wordt gehouden door het SBNL Natuurfonds. Met de prijs wil het fonds aandacht vestigen op mooie, bijzondere of monumentale bomen, of bomen die van betekenis voor de omgeving en de gemeenschap zijn. Vorig jaar werd de mammoetboom in het Abraham Ledeboerpark in Enschede uitgeroepen tot Boom van het Jaar . De beuk werd in een voorronde al verkozen tot de mooiste boom van de provincie Groningen. In de landelijke finale werd 6721 keer op de boom gestemd, schrijft RTV Noord . Hopen op nakomelingen Lid van de plaatselijke kerkcommissie Mark van Dijken kijkt met een dubbel gevoel naar de prijs: "Onze rode beuk heeft het best moeilijk. Kijk maar eens hoeveel beukennootjes er liggen. Hij maakt er extra veel aan, in de hoop op nakomelingen." Volgens Miriam van der Waart, groenmanager bij Groninger Kerken, hebben de beuken op het kerkhof van Middelstum te lijden onder langdurige droogte en veranderende klimaatomstandigheden. "Juist daarom is deze erkenning zo bijzonder. Het laat zien hoeveel deze boom voor Middelstum betekent, maar ook hoe kwetsbaar ons groene erfgoed is", zegt Van der Waart.

Integrating MaxEnt and MaxNet for climate-resilient habitat restoration: Predicting the ecological niche of Eucalyptus tereticornis in semi-arid landscapes
items.samenvatting_bron: by Pavan Kumar, Megha Paul, Preeti Kumari, Manmohan Dobriyal, Pankaj Lavania, Manish Srivastav, Prem Chandra Pandey, Benson Turyasingura Accurate modeling of species distribution is essential for effective biodiversity conservation, afforestation planning, and land-use management. This study presents a comparative analysis of two prominent presence-only species distribution models Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) and MaxNet to evaluate their efficacy in predicting the ecological niche of Eucalyptus tereticornis in a semi-arid agro-climatic region. A total of 138 georeferenced occurrence records and 25 pseudo-absence points were used, incorporating key environmental variables such as wind speed, temperature range, precipitation, and root zone soil wetness. Both models were optimized and assessed using metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and the Area Under the Curve (AUC). Results indicate that MaxEnt outperformed MaxNet in most metrics, achieving an accuracy of 87.5% and an AUC of 0.956, compared to MaxNet’s accuracy of 75% and AUC of 0.926. Environmental variable importance varied by model, with MaxEnt highlighting surface pressure and MaxNet emphasizing wind speed. Probability density plots revealed that MaxEnt distinctly identified high suitability zones, whereas MaxNet offered a more balanced, conservative distribution across the landscape. Het resultaat daarvan was dat de reserveringstermijnen sinds het voorjaar van 2021 hoger waren dan gewenst (met een piek in het voorjaar van 2022). Het terugdringen van de reserveringstermijnen naar het reguliere niveau (kpi is maximaal 7 weken voor een eerste B-examen en maximaal 5 weken voor een herexamen B) is lastig gebleken. Ondanks het massaal werven van nieuwe examinatoren, het maximaliseren van overwerk en de inzet van gepensioneerde examinatoren nam de reserveringstermijn weliswaar af, maar was het tempo (te) laag. In januari 2025 is daarom besloten om de tussentijdse toets (TTT) per 1 april 2025 tijdelijk niet aan te bieden. Een besluit dat niet gemakkelijk genomen werd, omdat de TTT een krachtig instrument is dat tot hogere slagingspercentages leidt omdat kandidaten goed voorbereid beginnen aan een examen. document.tekst_begin: Aanleiding De Tweede Kamer heeft schriftelijke vragen gesteld over de ontwerpbegroting 2027 Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties (VII). Bij dezen leggen wij u de beantwoording voor. Uiterlijk 22 oktober wenst de Kamer de beantwoording te ontvangen. Geadviseerd besluit • Akkoord gaan met de beantwoording op de schriftelijke Kamervragen over de ontwerpbegroting 2027 Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties. • MinBZK: De aanbiedingsbrief ondertekenen. Indien u opmerkingen hebt bij de voorliggende beantwoording, zullen wij deze opmerkingen verwerken en de beantwoording opnieuw aan u voorleggen. Kern Er zijn 105 vragen gesteld over de ontwerpbegroting 2027 van BZK. De vragen gaan met name over Herstel Groningen, lokale bestuurders, beleidsdoelen in de begroting, taakstellingen, FIMI-detectie en discriminatie. Ook zijn er enkele vragen over externe inhuur, vergunningsaanvragen, de taskforces, democratie, het gemeenschapsfonds, de budgetflexibiliteit van een aantal begrotingsartikelen en over het slavernijverleden. Toelichting Deze schriftelijke vragen zijn gesteld in de aanloop naar de begrotingsbehandeling van BZK op 3 en 5 november. De Kamer heeft ook schriftelijke vragen gestel

document.tekst_begin: Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal 2 Vergaderjaar 2025–2026 36 835 Implementatie van Richtlijn (EU) 2024/1712 van het Europees Parlement en de Raad van 13 juni 2024 tot wijziging van Richtlijn 2011/36/EU inzake de voorkoming en bestrijding van mensenhandel en de bescherming van slachtoffers daarvan (Implementatiewet herziene Europese richtlijn mensenhandel) Nr. 8 AMENDEMENT VAN HET LID FABER Ontvangen 24 augustus 2026 De ondergetekende stelt het volgende amendement voor: Voor de punt aan het slot van artikel I, onderdeel A, wordt ingevoegd «, en wordt aan dat lid toegevoegd «, alsmede het door een ouder vooruit- sturen van een alleenstaande minderjarige vreemdeling met het oogmerk als ouder van dat kind een verblijfsrecht te verwerven krachtens artikel 29c, eerste lid, onderdeel c, van de Vreemdelingenwet 2000»». Toelichting Indiener wil als extra categorie van uitbuiting toevoegen aan artikel 273f van het Wetboek van Strafrecht het door de ouder(s) vooruitsturen van een minderjarig kind naar Nederland. Het kind wordt misbruikt door de ouders, doordat zij uit eigen gewin het lot van hun eigen minderjarige kind in handen leggen van het circuit van mensensmokkelaars en mensenhandelaars

document.tekst_begin: Onderzoek Dure Casuïstiek Jeugdwet Ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport Directie Jeugd 15-09-2026 Management samenvatting Aanleiding Om de doorontwikkeling van de financiële systematiek binnen de Jeugdwet te ondersteunen, is inzicht nodig in de omvang en financiële impact van dure casuïstiek. Dit onderzoek brengt deze casuïstiek voor het eerst op landelijke schaal in beeld en laat zien welke invloed zij heeft op de jeugdzorguitgaven van gemeenten. De resultaten bieden een feitelijke basis voor het vervolg van de discussie over de verdeling van middelen binnen de Jeugdwet. Het onderzoek is beschrijvend van aard en doet geen uitspraken over beleidskeuzes of aanpassingen van de financieringssystematiek. Belangrijkste bevindingen Een beperkte groep jeugdigen legt een steeds groter beslag op de totale jeugdzorguitgaven. Het aantal jeugdigen met jaarlijkse jeugdzorguitgaven boven €100.000 is naar schatting gestegen van circa 5.400 in 2022 naar circa 9.600 in 2024. De bijbehorende uitgaven namen toe van circa €780 miljoen naar circa €1,66 miljard. document.tekst_begin: Bestuurlijke uitgangspunten rondom voorkomen en verkorten van open residentiële jeugdhulp Opgave Jeugdigen zo thuis mogelijk laten opgroeien is een belangrijke opgave binnen de jeugdhulp waar partijen, vanuit hun eigen rol en verantwoordelijkheid, de afgelopen jaren op hebben ingezet. Afhankelijk van de situatie, kan zo thuis mogelijk er op verschillende manieren uitzien. Idealiter groeien jeugdigen in hun eigen thuissituatie op, met ambulante hulp indien nodig. Als dat niet lukt, spelen pleegzorg en gezinshuizen in de regio een belangrijke rol om jeugdigen een thuis te bieden. Wanneer residentiële jeugdhulp toch noodzakelijk is, willen we dat dit deel uitmaakt van een ambulant traject: tijdelijk en gericht op zo snel mogelijk terug naar thuis. Binnen residentieel verblijf wordt een veilig en positief leefklimaat én maatwerk geboden. We zetten maximaal in op het voorkomen van verhuizingen. Dit heeft een groot ontwrichtend effect op jongeren. In de Hervormingsagenda is het belang van zo thuis mogelijk opgroeien voor jeugdigen opnieuw onderstreept. items.titel: A harmonized individual-level phytoplankton trait dataset from Mediterranean and Black Sea transitional waters
items.samenvatting_bron: Transitional waters are dynamic coastal ecosystems located at the interface between freshwater and marine environments. They are characterized by pronounced environmental variability resulting from the interaction between geomorphology, freshwater inputs, tidal exchanges, climatic variability, and human activities. These factors generate high habitat heterogeneity and complex ecological dynamics. Phytoplankton communities inhabiting transitional waters are particularly sensitive to both natural gradients and anthropogenic pressures, often exhibiting marked spatial and seasonal patterns in species composition, abundance and functional structure. In response to fluctuating environmental conditions, phytoplankton taxa display a wide range of morphometric and functional adaptations, making trait-based approaches especially suitable for investigating community organization and ecosystem functioning in these ecosystems. Although a large amount of phytoplankton trait data is available, its use could be enhanced through improved data harmonization and interoperability. The availability of FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable) phytoplankton trait data from transitional waters, coupled with associated environmental information, is therefore essential to support comparative analyses and to improve our understanding of trait–environment relationships in these vulnerable ecosystems. items.titel: Beyond channel count: metrological performance metrics for compact multi-channel spectral sensors
items.samenvatting_bron: Compact multi-channel spectral sensors based on thin-film interference filters offer a low-cost, integrable alternative to dispersive spectrometers, yet their performance is too often assessed by channel count alone, an indicator blind to inter-channel crosstalk, filter bandwidth, and the underdetermined nature of the spectral measurement. We present a metrological framework that formalises the channel-wise measurement model, identifies the dominant Type B instrumental uncertainty contributions (interference-filter centre-wavelength tolerance, responsivity line-shape deviation, PGA gain tolerance, and ADC quantisation and noise), and propagates them from the digital-count domain to irradiance through the device calibration curve. From the same datasheet parameters, the framework derives two figures of merit: the inter-channel crosstalk matrix C and the effective number of independent measurements Meff, obtained as the participation ratio of the eigenvalues of C. The uncertainty budget is developed in detail for the AS7343, a device with broad and overlapping filters, under three calibration scenarios of increasing effort, while the figures of merit are computed for both the AS7341 and the AS7343. Predictions are cross-validated against the experimental spectral reconstruction errors reported in our previous calibration study on xenon illuminants. items.titel: Integrating temperature and CO2-concentration impact on crops into an input–output framework
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Environmental Input–Output Analysis (IOA) incorporates feedbacks in coupled economic-environmental systems, driven by an exogenous demand and fixed input–output coefficients with a linearity assumption. For some environmental problems, or over longer time periods, the IO coefficients and exogenous drivers may change. Here, we introduce a climate-feedback into an IO system via the crop sector to illustrate the potential couplings between climate change and material and economic flows. We use existing climate impact ensembles to calibrate climate feedback parameters for crop productivity and implement them in an expanded IO system. We generally find that the same exogenous demand can be met with lower output due to yield improvements, driven by the beneficial effect of CO 2 fertilization which generally dominates the modelled temperature effect on yield, essentially indicating a reduction in land-use intensity driven by CO2 fertilization. However, the temperature effect, which is positive or negative dependent on region, may be underestimated because of the inability of existing process-based models to simulate climate-related agricultural impacts. The overall changes in yield, when exogenous demand is held fixed and annual CO 2 emissions are used as feedback, are of the order of 0.2% when normalized with the regional crop outputs and much smaller when normalized with total output. items.titel: Feasibility study of using magnetic and thermoelectric methods for the assessment of storage-induced changes in flux-cored welding wires
items.samenvatting_bron: The lack of knowledge regarding whether a welding consumable remains suitable for the welding process or has undergone degradation that precludes its further use constitutes a significant challenge. Appropriate control procedures and effective evaluation methods may contribute to addressing this issue. This study presents the results of investigations concerning the applicability of magnetic and thermoelectric methods for such an assessment. Rutile flux-cored welding wires were stored in four different locations and subsequently collected for testing after 3, 6, and 12 months. Their suitability for industrial application was initially assessed on the basis of visual examination. Subsequently, measurements of thermoelectric power, characterization of bulk magnetic properties, and Magnetic Barkhausen Noise (MBN) were performed for each wire. Visual inspection confirmed the good surface condition of the wires despite the exceedance of the recommended limits of temperature and relative humidity during storage. The thermoelectric measurements showed that storage environment significantly affects the Seebeck Coefficient (SC) of welding wires, with marine conditions inducing rapid changes and less aggressive environments producing a gradual time dependent increase. Magnetic property measurements indicated that two of the evaluated parameters, namely the amplitude of MBN and the area under the envelopes of MBN, exhibited changes with storage time at each exposure site. items.titel: Coordination Competition Couples Oxygen Vacancy‐Rich SnO x With Isolated Cu–N Sites for CO 2 ‐to‐formate Electroreduction
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Selective CO 2 ‐to‐formate electroreduction requires oxygen‐deficient SnO x sites that stabilize O‐bound * OCHO intermediates while resisting cathodic over‐reduction. Here, we use a precursor‐level coordination competition strategy to construct an oxygen vacancy (O v )‐rich SnO x catalyst coupled with isolated Cu–N sites through controlled conversion of amino‐functionalized Cu/Sn metal‐organic frameworks. Competitive coordination of Cu and Sn with 2‐aminoterephthalic acid (H 2 BDC‐NH 2 ) is associated with altered precursor growth and a heterogeneous local environment, favoring the formation of defective SnO x domains during thermal conversion while enabling ligand‐derived nitrogen sites to anchor redistributed Cu species. Spectroscopic investigations reveal that the optimized Cu‐SnO x /NC catalyst contains abundant vacancy‐related SnO x environments and predominantly isolated Cu–N configurations, which are associated with stabilized O‐bound * OCHO intermediates and mitigated cathodic reconstruction of SnO x . Operando Raman spectroscopy further indicates persistent formate‐related intermediates and comparatively lower bicarbonate accumulation during CO 2 electroreduction. Consequently, Cu‐SnO x /NC achieves a formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96% at −100 mA cm −2 and maintains efficiencies above 85% over a moderate current density range in both alkaline and neutral electrolytes. items.titel: Magnetically Induced Functional Fe 3 O 4 /Iron Foam Catalysts for Enhanced CO 2 ‐Assisted Ethane Dehydrogenation
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT CO 2 ‐assisted ethane dehydrogenation (CO 2 ‐EDH) combines olefin production with CO 2 conversion, yet suffers from high temperatures and catalyst instability in thermal catalysis. This work establishes an alternating current magnetic field (ACMF)‐mediated catalytic system using Fe 3 O 4 decorated on iron foam (Fe 3 O 4 /IF) as the induction catalyst, achieving significant enhancement of the CO 2 ‐EDH process under mild conditions. At 500°C, a temperature 200°C lower than that required in conventional thermal catalysis to reach a comparable conversion level, the system realized an ethane conversion of 22.2% with 97% ethylene selectivity. At an equivalent conversion level, the catalyst stability was improved by 15‐fold compared to traditional thermal catalysis, with continuous stable operation for 80 h. The eddy current effect induced by the alternating magnetic field promotes electron transfer between Fe and Fe 3 O 4 and accelerates the oxygen redox cycle, thereby enhancing the reaction kinetics of the CO 2 ‐EDH process based on the Mars–van Krevelen (MvK) mechanism. This work provides an effective approach for improving the performance of alkane dehydrogenation under mild conditions and contributes new insights to the field of magnetically induced catalysis.

items.titel: Engineering a Modular Bacterial Galactose Oxidase through CBM Recombination and Second-Shell Substitutions
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Galactose oxidases (GalOxs) are copper-radical enzymes that selectively oxidize primary alcohols, yet the structure–function determinants governing their catalytic efficiency and substrate scope remain incompletely understood, particularly in bacterial enzymes. Here, we combine biochemical and structural characterization with directed evolution of PsGalOx from Pseudarthrobacter siccitolerans. Spectroscopic analysis showed that PsGalOx can form the catalytically competent Cu(II)–tyrosyl radical state. The enzyme also displays an unusual modular architecture comprising two tandem carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs). The enzyme preferentially oxidizes d-galactose and d-galactose-containing oligo- and polysaccharides. Functional analyses reveal distinct roles for the two CBM32 domains: CBM32-I enhances polysaccharide binding but limits soluble expression, whereas CBM32-II primarily contributes to protein stability. During directed evolution with d-galactose, recombination between the homologous CBMs generated chimeric single-CBM variants enriched primarily through increased soluble production rather than intrinsic catalytic improvement. Subsequent screening with benzyl alcohol as a model noncarbohydrate substrate selected second-shell substitutions near the copper center that increased intrinsic catalytic turnover and broadened substrate scope. items.titel: Efficient Separation of Xe/Kr by Induced Polarization on Single‐Atom Modified Ti 3 C 2 O 2 : A DFT Study
items.samenvatting_bron: The efficient separation of radioactive xenon (Xe) and krypton (Kr) is challenging due to their similar sizes and chemical inertness. To address this, dispersing metal atoms as single sites on a substrate can utilize their highly localized electronic structure and concentrated charge to enhance polarization of noble gas atoms, thereby achieving effective Xe/Kr adsorption and separation. Two‐dimensional MXene materials, with their large specific surface areas and tunable surface terminal groups, offer promising substrates for supporting metal atoms. In this study, we performed ab initio density functional theory (DFT) calculations to systematically evaluate the adsorption and separation capabilities of transition metal (TM) functionalized Ti 3 C 2 O 2 (TM‐Ti 3 C 2 O 2 ) for Xe and Kr. Among the tested metals, Cu–Ti 3 C 2 O 2 exhibited the strongest adsorption toward both gases. Charge density difference and partial density of states analyses revealed that the supported Cu atom induce significant polarization of Xe and Kr, facilitating pronounced interactions between the p orbitals of the gas atoms and the d orbitals of Cu. Furthermore, Cu–Ti 3 C 2 O 2 showed the largest difference in adsorption energy between Xe and Kr, demonstrating its strong potential as an effective material for Xe/Kr separation.

items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Methylene blue poses different health risks to humans and harms the environment. The current research developed a hybrid adsorbent combining gallic acid and tin oxide, with the addition of activated carbon, to mitigate the detrimental impact of methylene blue effluent pollution. The adsorptive characteristics of GA@SnO 2 -AC were validated using the point of zero charge, SEM-EDX, FTIR, and TGA. The variables that determine dye adsorption were examined. The highest adsorption capacity of 95.24 mg/g was achieved. The experiment data matched with Langmuir model and PSO, indicating the applicability of the MB dye uptake. The R L values range from 0.6880 to 0.7280, suggesting a favourable process. Thermodynamic investigation showed negative values for ΔH o (-23.1196) and ΔS o (-0.0442), indicating an exothermic adsorption system with random subsidence by adsorbed species. items.titel: γ‐Radionuclide Technetium‐99M Activated Long‐Lasting Chemodynamic Therapy and Immunogenic Brachytherapy for Enhanced Antitumor Immunity
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Chemodynamic therapy (CDT) and brachytherapy face critical challenges, particularly the limited efficiency of Fenton reaction and the insufficient antitumor immunogenicity of brachytherapy. In this study, we employ the metal–organic framework nanocomposite Hf‐TCPP@Fe‐ 99m Tc (where TCPP = tetrakis(4‐carboxyphenyl) porphyrin and 99m Tc = technetium‐99m) for synergistic long‐lasting CDT and immunogenic brachytherapy. Benefiting from the robust interaction between 99m Tc‐emitted γ‐rays and the high‐Z element Hf, the secondary electrons generated during brachytherapy not only damage tumor cells but also establish an electron‐rich microenvironment that drives the continuous reduction of Fe 3+ to Fe 2+ , thereby sustaining a highly efficient Fenton reaction. With the generation of hydroxyl radical persisting for over 12 h, this synergistic effect reduced cell viability by an additional 28.6% beyond projections, thereby inducing effective immunogenic cell death, activating a systemic antitumor immune response, and inhibiting both primary and metastatic triple‐negative breast cancer. Through rational design, this work demonstrates that clinically prevalent nontherapeutic γ‐radionuclide can activate long‐lasting CDT and immunogenic brachytherapy to enhance antitumor immunogenicity.

items.titel: A Comprehensive Review and Future Prospects of Aluminum–Sulfur Batteries: From Material Design to Practical Challenges
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Aluminum–sulfur (Al–S) batteries are promising next‐generation energy storage systems owing to the high abundance, low cost, and multi‐electron redox capability of Al, combined with the high theoretical capacity and environmental friendliness of S. This review systematically compares the dual electrochemical mechanisms based on S reduction (S 0 /S 2− ) and S oxidation (S 0 /S 4+ ), highlighting their distinct advantages in energy density and safety. Key strategies for cathode design—including carbon‐based, anchoring‐functional, and catalytic‐functional hosts—are discussed, alongside electrolyte engineering using ionic liquids, deep eutectic solvents, inorganic molten salts, and aqueous systems. Recent advances in dendrite suppression, anode protective layers, and functional separators are also summarized. A central challenge identified is the sluggish Al 3+ solvation/desolvation kinetics, which limits rate capability and low‐temperature performance. The application of in situ/operando characterization techniques (XANES, Raman, UV–vis) to unravel complex reaction pathways is emphasized. By integrating multidisciplinary innovations, this review provides a comprehensive perspective and a phased commercialization roadmap, aiming to accelerate the transition of Al–S batteries from laboratory research to practical green energy storage.

items.samenvatting_bron: Microplastics (MPs) have transitioned from a predominantly marine concern to a defining threat facing terrestrial agroecosystems, where croplands now function as one of the largest global reservoirs of plastic particles. items.titel: Development and application of an analytical method for the quantification of tire wear in atmospheric deposition
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract. Tire wear particles (TWP) are a major source of microplastic pollution and a carrier of rubber additives and metal-containing compounds that can be released into the environment and adversely affect ecosystems. Reliable quantification of TWP remains challenging because tire materials are compositionally heterogeneous and environmental samples contain complex organic and inorganic matrices that interfere with their analysis. Here, we present a pyrolysis-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (Py-GC-MS) method for the quantification of TWP in atmospheric deposition samples. The method combines targeted sample pretreatment, including density separation and removal of organic matrix components, with the analysis of six characteristic pyrolysis products of tire rubber, namely butadiene, 4-vinylcyclohexene, isoprene, limonene, styrene, and α-methylstyrene. The sum of the integrated peak areas of these markers is used to quantify TWP mass. Instrumental parameters, including pyrolysis temperature (set to 500 °C) and gas chromatographic separation, were systematically optimized to maximize sensitivity, reproducibility, and chromatographic resolution. Calibration was established using cryo-milled tread materials from 23 used passenger car and truck/bus tires as well as a mixture of cryo-milled tread materials representative of the U.S. tire market. The sum of the six marker signals showed a strong linear relationship with tire tread mass across different tire types (r² = 0.93).

items.titel: Regulation strategies of atom economy for iron-based catalysts in syngas catalytic conversion
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract As a key evaluation metric for direct catalytic syngas conversion, hydrogen atom economy or carbon atom economy can accurately quantify the different atom flows during the main and side reactions, which would provide new insight for the rational design. This work reviewed the active phase types, structural evolution patterns, and regulatory mechanisms for syngas conversion on iron-based catalysts. On this basis, it elaborated the optimization paths of carbon and hydrogen atom economies and analyzed the coupling and trade-offs. It was pointed out that the balance of hydrogen atom economy and carbon atom economy was the goal for improving the atomic utilization efficiency in iron-based catalytic syngas conversion. Moreover, the appropriate application of interdisciplinary strategies could open up new perspectives for the efficient regulation of atom economy and provide novel insights for developing high-performance catalytic systems.

items.titel: Pyrolysis temperature controls the accessible pore volume and capric acid encapsulation efficiency of coconut shell biochar
items.samenvatting_bron: Waste-derived biochar is a low-cost scaffold for shape-stabilized phase change materials (PCMs), yet how pyrolysis temperature governs the pore volume a molten PCM can reach remains unresolved. Here we decouple surface area from pore accessibility by preparing ZnCl 2 -activated coconut shell biochars at 550, 700, 850 and 1000 °C under an identical protocol and impregnating them with capric acid. Contrary to the assumption that higher BET surface area guarantees greater PCM loading, encapsulation efficiency tracks the pore volume accessible on the adsorption branch. Between the 850 and 1000 °C biochars the BET area differs by only 3.3%, whereas the BJH adsorption cumulative pore volume differs by 17.6% (0.1102 versus 0.1296 cm 3 g –1 ) and the encapsulation efficiency by 18.5% (57.59 versus 68.25%). High-resolution TEM resolves the origin: short, curved graphene fringes constrict pore entrances at 850 °C, whereas extended parallel stacks bound open channels at 1000 °C. Efficiency rises from 42.25% at 550 °C to 68.25% at 1000 °C; the optimized composite delivers 112.88 J g –1 , does not leak at 55 °C and retains 99% of its latent heat after 500 cycles. Accessible pore volume, not surface area, is the key design criterion for biochar PCMs in passive building thermal regulation.

items.titel: A renaissance of pseudosands: on improving the understanding of soil architecture in deeply weathered soils
items.samenvatting_bron: Soil texture, the most widely used soil property to describe single grain size distribution, is different from soil structure. Setting them equal neglects the impact of actual particle arrangements under natural conditions. Particularly in deeply weathered soils, the mismatch between soil texture and structure has widely been described. It is therefore not surprising, that biogeochemical models built on texture-based assumptions systematically diverge from field observations, for example, often overestimating nitrous oxide emission rates. Water-stable aggregates like pseudosands, often described for deeply weathered soils, might be responsible for this mismatch. In the field they are perceived as sand, but in laboratory analysis for texture determination measured as clay and silt. This thesis develops pseudosands as a tractable entry point into studying aggregate stability and pore space as complementary aspects of soil structure. An initial literature review revealed a persistent lack of consistent classification for pseudosands, hindering comparison across studies. However, when looking for water-stable aggregation in literature, dynamic water balances emerge as the most determining pattern for their global distribution. items.titel: Positively Charged Hollow Fiber Nanofiltration Membrane With an SPSf / PEI Bilayer Prepared via Dip‐Coating
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Nanofiltration (NF) has attracted considerable interest in water purification and resource recovery. Hollow fiber membranes offer high packing density, large surface‐area‐to‐volume ratio, and low‐pressure high‐flux operation. However, the fabrication of hollow fiber NF membranes often suffers from non‐uniform and discontinuous separation layers, while most conventional NF membranes are negatively charged and inclined to fouling caused by the adsorption of positively charged ions. In this work, a positively charged hollow fiber NF membrane was fabricated by constructing a sulfonated polysulfone (SPSf)/polyethyleneimine (PEI) electrostatic assembly bilayer via dip‐coating. The SPSf interlayer was first coated onto the polyethersulfone (PES) surface to enhance interfacial adhesion, facilitate PEI assembly, and prevent excessive PEI penetration into the membrane pores, thereby forming a dense, defect‐free selective layer via electrostatic interactions. The PES/SPSf‐PEI membrane showed high rejection for MgCl 2 (90.96%), crystal violet (99.56%), and rhodamine B (99.81%). Moreover, a flux recovery ratio of 86.77% was achieved after three fouling‐cleaning cycles using rhodamine B as a model foulant. This work provides a facile and controllable approach for preparing high‐performance positively charged hollow fiber NF membranes, showing great potential for divalent cation rejection and dye treatment.

items.titel: Massively Multiplexed Photonic Chip With Cross‐Channel Fusion For Harmonized Biosensing
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Accurate, label‐free analysis of complex biological mixtures is limited by poor multiplexing scalability and inconsistent responses across sensor samples. We introduce a transformative sensing platform that integrates large‐scale photonic multiplexing with data‐driven analytics to overcome these constraints. Our modular, affordable glass‐chip whispering–gallery–mode (WGM) photonic architecture is designed to support simultaneous readout of up to 100 sensing channels comprising over 10 000 high‐Q microresonators, exceeding existing multiplexing capabilities by more than two orders of magnitude. The photonic system is reinforced by the novel, cross‐platform, deep learning framework BioCCF. It applies cross‐channel fusion in biosensing for the first time and enables harmonized operation across heterogeneous chips by leveraging domain adaptation. Using over 200 h of measurements from nine independent chips, we demonstrate chip‐independent multiplexed biosensing with 99.3% identification accuracy and relative quantification errors of 10 for immunoglobulin G mixtures. Beyond this validation, the platform supports multi‐analyte immunoassays, environmental monitoring, and distributed diagnostics, enabling aligned sensor networks with shared data infrastructures and continuously improving generalization of the common analyzing framework.

items.titel: A harmonized database of biosphere–atmosphere ammonia flux measurements across ecosystems and pollution regimes
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Ammonia (NH 3 ) is a trace gas with detrimental effects on human health and ecosystems. Understanding and quantification of NH 3 exchange between the biosphere and atmosphere is essential for assessing ecosystem nitrogen budgets and critical load exceedances. Yet, uncertainty in these processes remains significant, due to the global scarcity of measurements. We created a database of more than 40,000 records of NH 3 flux measurements across ecosystems, including heathlands, peatlands, grasslands, forests, croplands, and dunes, in areas with varying ambient NH 3 and sulphur dioxide concentrations, using different measurement techniques from 1991 to 2024. A significant share of measurements originates from the Netherlands, reflecting its early deployment of a high-resolution NH 3 monitoring network. Fluxes are quality controlled and harmonized using consistent algorithms, with uncertainty estimates included. Fluxes were recalculated using consistent stability correction functions, ensuring comparability across sites. By providing this database, we aim to contribute to the understanding of the NH 3 biosphere-atmosphere exchange, its environmental controls, the validation and calibration of NH 3 exchange schemes, and the characterization of NH 3 fluxes across ecosystems.

items.titel: Plant invasions are associated with lower community stability at multiple spatial scales
items.samenvatting_bron: Plant invasions are threatening the long-term sustainability of ecosystem functions. Yet, how plant invasions impact the temporal stability of community cover across spatial scales remains poorly understood, hindering effective invasion management. Using the National Ecological Observatory Network dataset, we examine how plant invasions influence multi-scale stability of total community abundance (used total community cover) via altering community functional diversity, as well as growth and dispersal strategies. We find that invasion-associated losses of functional α diversity and functional shifts toward acquisitive strategies, reduce species asynchrony and species stability, respectively. These changes ultimately lead to lower temporal stability at the local scale (α stability). Meanwhile, invasion-associated functional shifts toward acquisitive seed dispersal strategies weaken functional β diversity, which reduces asynchrony community dynamics among local communities (spatial asynchrony). These concurrent declines in α stability and spatial asynchrony collectively destabilize metacommunity-scale stability. Our findings reveal that plant invasions may trigger destabilizing effects across spatial scales, associated with changes in functional diversity as well as growth and dispersal strategies, underscoring the need for a multi-scale invasion management framework focusing on both local diversity and the connectivity among local communities. items.titel: Human-centred design approaches to tsunami mitigation under sea level rise in Kesennuma, Japan
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract. Human-centred design (HCD) is increasingly prioritised as studies show human experience is critical in infrastructure use, and recent policies call for more socially responsive design. Tsunami impacts intensify as sea level rise (SLR) raises baseline water levels and reduces existing defence effectiveness, yet HCD informed approaches are rarely tested under projected SLR. Based on identified infrastructure preferences in Kesennuma City, Japan, we develop three multi-layered defence configurations: an environmentally integrated eco hybrid system (Design 1), a discreet open feeling barrier system (Design 2), and a reinforced high-performance system (Design 3). Using TUNAMI-N2 numerical modelling, 150 simulations combine three tsunami sources, five SLR conditions, and five defence states. Results for inundation extent, fatality rates, and economic loss show a consistent hierarchy: Design 3 achieves the strongest containment, while Design 2, which more closely aligns with residents’ preferences for openness and access, delivers near equivalent reductions typically within 10–15 percent. Design 1 provides only limited hazard reduction and is unsuitable as a standalone mitigation system. We show that HCD informed configurations can deliver strong technical performance and support a shift toward socially integrated, multi-layered tsunami protection under rising sea levels.

items.titel: Toward Sustainable Climate Governance: How Economic, Technological, and Geopolitical Factors Shape Environmental Policy Stringency
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT This paper examines the effect of environmental pressure, geopolitical risk, technological innovation, economic growth, and urbanization on Environmental Policy Stringency (EPS) of E7 economies for the period 1992–2024. The main estimator is MMQR, and the other estimators are AMG, CCEMG, and median IVQR. The MMQR results demonstrate that technical innovation is positively and strongly related to EPS in all the quantiles considered, with larger coefficients in the higher quantiles. We find positive and significant relationships between economic growth and urbanization at upper quantiles, and modest negative associations between carbon emissions and higher quantiles. Geopolitical risk has mostly insignificant relationships. AMG and CCEMG studies provide complementary data on technological innovation and carbon emissions, whereas the IVQR results further strengthen the positive innovation‐EPS association. The current study adds to the existing body of evidence by investigating EPS as an effect of economic, technological, environmental, and geopolitical factors in rising economies via a distributional framework. The results of the study show the significance of technology capacity and regulatory circumstances adapted to the context for environmental governance, providing insights pertinent to SDG 9, SDG 11, and SDG 13.

items.titel: Hybrid water security governance after conflict in South Sudan
items.samenvatting_bron: This paper examines the hybrid institutional arrangements governing water security in post-conflict South Sudan. Based on a qualitative comparative case study of two sub-national states, it analyses how formal state agencies, customary authorities, and non-governmental organisations negotiate authority over water resources in practice. The findings reveal a landscape where customary systems, led by chiefs and water custodians, exercise primary de facto control over access and management, often operating in parallel to or in tension with a weak formal state apparatus. This hybridity manifests in both collaborative and conflictual interactions, directly shaping—and often entrenching—differentiated access along social and ethnic lines. Theoretically, the study advances the concept of hybrid governance by demonstrating how these emergent systems critically determine the delivery of an essential resource, moving analysis beyond a narrow focus on political or security institutions. It concludes that water governance serves as a microcosm of South Sudan's contested statebuilding, where multiple sources of legitimacy coexist. For policymakers, the analysis underscores the necessity of engaging constructively with existing hybrid orders rather than imposing external, state-centric blueprints.

items.titel: With whom you elaborate matters: how learning orientation impacts cross-culture and same-culture information elaboration in culturally diverse teams
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Work teams are increasingly characterized by diverse cultural backgrounds. Although research has established that cultural diversity holds the potential to enhance team performance through information elaboration—the exchange, discussion, and integration of task-relevant information—prior work has treated elaboration as an undifferentiated process, leaving unspecified whether it occurs across or within cultural boundaries. We develop a differentiated elaboration perspective that distinguishes cross-culture information elaboration between culturally dissimilar members from same-culture information elaboration between culturally similar members. Using a multi-source, multi-wave study of 104 culturally diverse teams comprising 587 members, we found that, as expected, cross-culture elaboration was more strongly related to team performance than same-culture elaboration. Moreover, team learning orientation predicted both forms of elaboration, and its indirect association with team performance was stronger through cross-culture elaboration. These findings advance a differentiated elaboration perspective to demonstrate that elaboration that crosses cultural boundaries is more important for diverse teams than same-culture elaboration. This points to opportunities for future research on reaping the benefits of diverse teams.

items.samenvatting_bron: Contemporary interest in glocalisation partly reflects the limitations of earlier globalising movements in medical education. The former evolves to a process through which globally-informed educational models are negotiated and reconstituted within local contexts. While global standards can enhance graduate mobility, implementation may privilege Western assumptions regarding competence, professionalism, and quality. This can lead to obscuration of local values, needs and realities. Existing scholarship has examined glocalisation through sociocultural and postcolonial perspectives, generating insights into issues of hierarchy, power, and culture. items.titel: Is China’s GDP undervalued? A digital economy model
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Transactions in a digital economy generate data that firms accumulate but national accounts do not price. Within the model developed here, that omission implies measured GDP understates output. We adapt the recursive data-economy framework of Farboodi and Veldkamp (2026) to China and construct a bottom-up measure of digital investment from the itemized asset disclosures of 5,120 listed firms. The model does not identify a unique asset perimeter, so we carry two measurement boundaries throughout rather than designating one as the headline. For 2024 the adjustment is 1.60% of GDP, or 2.16 trillion RMB, under a broad boundary that includes telecommunications network assets, and 0.60%, or 0.82 trillion RMB, under a narrow boundary that excludes them. These are alternative measurement boundaries, not statistical bounds. On listed firms alone, before any extrapolation to unlisted firms, the broad-boundary figure is 0.91%. Because the knowledge stock is not identified without forecast-error data, the broad-boundary figure carries a calibrated scenario range of 0.77–4.07%, which reflects alternative calibrations rather than sampling uncertainty. Every figure is conditional on a normalization of the mapping between measured digital investment and the value of data. A validation audit of the classifier uncovers measurement defects that are not specific to China.

items.titel: Architecting Anode Current Collectors for Practical Anode-Free Alkali Metal Batteries
items.samenvatting_bron: Anode-free alkali metal batteries (AFAMBs) are emerging as a compelling strategy to surpass the cell-level energy density limits of Li-ion batteries while simplifying battery configuration. In these systems, the working anode forms in situ on a bare current collector and is continuously reshaped during cycling with a limited alkali metal inventory. As a result, the anode current collector is not merely a passive electron conductor, but a multifunctional interfacial platform that governs alkali metal nucleation, growth, stripping, and interphase evolution. This review examines the fundamental differences among anode-free lithium, sodium, and potassium systems and highlights key performance metrics for practical AFAMBs. Recent current collector engineering strategies developed for these chemistries are then summarized. Essential parameters shaping current collector design are identified, including electronic conductivity, alkali metal affinity, collector morphology, and interphase stability. Finally, practical design principles are presented to balance electrochemical performance with manufacturability under realistic operating conditions. This review aims to clarify the alkali metal-dependent design logic of current collectors and to provide guidance for the practical development of next-generation anode-free batteries.

items.titel: Building Predictive Identity Threat Models Using Behavioral Biometrics and Zero Trust Cybersecurity Principles
items.samenvatting_bron: This review explores the integration of behavioral biometrics and Zero Trust cybersecurity principles in building predictive identity threat models for advanced cyber defense. As traditional perimeter-based security becomes increasingly ineffective against sophisticated identity-based attacks, the fusion of behavioral biometrics—such as keystroke dynamics, mouse movement, touchscreen behavior, and gait recognition—with Zero Trust frameworks offers a more dynamic and continuous method of user authentication and threat prediction. By leveraging machine learning algorithms to analyze behavioral patterns in real time, organizations can identify anomalies indicative of account compromise, insider threats, or unauthorized access. Zero Trust, which operates on the principle of “never trust, always verify,” ensures that every user and device is continuously authenticated, authorized, and validated based on risk context and behavioral insights. This paper synthesizes the state-of-the-art technologies, architectures, and analytical techniques underpinning predictive identity threat modeling. It also examines use cases across sectors, implementation challenges, and future directions for securing digital identities in an era of pervasive cyber threats.

items.titel: Data Annotation as Measurement
items.samenvatting_bron: Modern AI systems depend on annotated data, but annotation is rarely treated as the act of measurement that it is. Instead, annotation quality is commonly reduced to agreement: if multiple annotators assign the same annotation to a data instance, the annotations are taken to be high-quality. Yet agreement does not establish whether annotations validly capture the underlying concept they are meant to represent. In this paper, we argue that data annotation should be understood as a measurement problem. Like other forms of measurement, annotation requires defining a concept, operationalizing it through an instrument, applying that instrument, and evaluating the reliability and validity of the resulting measurements. Drawing on a literature review of annotation quality research (N=132) and semi-structured interviews with annotation team members (N=10), we develop a framework for diagnosing and correcting annotation issues. First, we map key decision points across annotation processes - including task design, annotator management, quality assessment, quality improvement, and adjudication - that shape annotation outcomes. Second, we identify five distinct sources of annotation issues: error, ambiguity, impossibility, subjectivity, and annotator identity. items.titel: Shaping the Future of Generative AI for Black Communities: A Frame Analysis of Public Discourse and Empirical Scholarly Research
items.samenvatting_bron: As generative AI (genAI) systems become embedded in education, employment, healthcare, and creative industries, the impact and engagement among marginalized groups have become both a widespread discourse and a focus in scholarly research. As a starting point, we examine public discourse and empirical research to explore the impact of genAI systems on Black communities. We conducted a systematic literature review (SLR) of 91 empirical papers alongside a media discourse frame analysis of 28 public resources, applying Entman's framing theory to map how each corpus defines problems, attributes causes, and proposes treatments. Our SLR reveals that scholarly research concentrates heavily on technical bias detection, reducing Blackness to measurable variables rather than engaging with cultural practices, structural conditions, or Black knowledge systems. Our frame analysis reveals that public discourse attributes genAI-related harm to historical and systemic forces, while scholarly research stops its causal accounts at the dataset and its treatment recommendations at technical reform. We demonstrate that this misalignment is structurally produced: anti-Blackness operates simultaneously across both registers, generating a shared evacuation of Black epistemic agency. We argue for frame analysis as an AI ethics methodology capable of surfacing what technical evaluation forecloses.

items.titel: Watermelon vine as dual-functional additive in ecological porous concrete
items.samenvatting_bron: Ecological porous concrete (EPC) is constrained by a persistent trade-off: the dense cementitious matrix required for strength reduces porosity and generates a highly alkaline pore environment (pH > 11) inimical to plant growth. To address this, the present study investigates watermelon vine (WV), an abundant agricultural waste, as a dual-functional additive that simultaneously provides physical reinforcement and chemical alkalinity regulation. An integrated orthogonal array–response surface methodology–entropy-weighted TOPSIS framework was established for multi-objective mix optimisation. WV content was identified as the dominant factor governing pore pH, reducing it to 7.6 at an optimal dosage of 3 wt% within 14 days. The optimised mix—comprising 16–20 mm coarse aggregate, 20 wt% fly ash, a water-to-binder ratio of 0.26, and 3 wt% WV—achieved a compressive strength of 10.4 MPa and an effective porosity of 27.7%, with compressive strength remaining stable at 60 d. Scanning electron microscopy revealed a dense interfacial transition zone containing crystalline products morphologically consistent with calcium oxalate, and plant germination tests confirmed vegetation establishment exceeding 80% coverage within 60 days. These converging lines of evidence support an in-situ acid–base neutralisation mechanism, positioning WV as a viable, low-cost functional resource for sustainable construction.

items.titel: Quantifying the contribution of vegetation layer uncertainty to simulated forest fuels treatment placement
items.samenvatting_bron: Background Western US forests face rising high-severity fire risk motivating increased investment in forest management. The high cost of treatments and vast areas needing work require efficient resource allocation. Forest landscape models can help scale up analysis and support management, but underlying uncertainties can limit their utility. Aims We examined uncertainty in the initial forest input layer, quantifying the error and determining how much field data are needed to produce outputs suitable for informing management. Methods We created eight initial forest layers using various sample sizes and selection methods, ran 50-year simulations and compared outputs. We also resampled model outputs from 100 to 500 m resolution and evaluated the effects. Key results Stratified sampling stabilized errors and allowed using smaller sample sizes relative to random sampling, and coarser resolution resampling reduced errors while retaining key information. Combining these strategies produced similar outputs using all and only 25% of the data. Conclusions Combining stratified sampling with output coarsening reduces data demands while maintaining analytical rigor, enabling more actionable guidance for management planning. Implications This work advances the operational use of landscape models as a decision-support tool, allowing managers to scale up planning by integrating model outputs with expert knowledge and reducing reliance on labor-intensive field inventories.

items.titel: Possibilities for strengthening nature experiences and nature stewardship in the ‘not yet engaged’
items.samenvatting_bron: It is commonly argued that encouraging people to spend time in nature and appreciate nature is an important conduit for encouraging engagement in conservation stewardship actions. However, there is limited data available to help us understand how those ‘not yet engaged’ in conservation actually perceive nature-based settings and possibilities for nature stewardship. Here we address this gap by recruiting ‘not yet engaged’ individuals and providing guided nature experiences, followed by in-situ interviews to examine participant perceptions of these nature experiences and stewardship actions. Qualitative analysis integrated Kellert’s value typology and Value‑Beliefs‑Norm theory to assess how nature was valued, and ‘ingredients’ for stewardship action. We found that all participants described a positive appreciation of nature, reflected by naturalistic and aesthetic value orientations. However, participants were less likely to demonstrate other ingredients for stewardship, including awareness of actions that they could perform, and sense of responsibility or moral obligation to take specific actions. These findings suggest that programs aiming to promote conservation actions should not rely on encouraging nature appreciation in isolation, but also foster awareness of available actions and a sense of personal responsibility.

items.titel: Habitat-use flexibility may promote the spread of Asian weatherloaches in Europe
items.samenvatting_bron: Asian weatherloaches have expanded their range across Europe, potentially increasing competitive pressure on the conservation-dependent native European weatherfish Misgurnus fossilis . Because interspecific interactions are potentially mediated by benthic habitat use, we quantified substrate choice of native European and invasive Asian weatherloaches in a replicated laboratory two-way choice experiment. Individual fish were tested in three sediment combinations (gravel/sand, gravel/mud, sand/mud) with four 60-min replicates per treatment and individual fish. Habitat use was quantified as the proportional time spent on each substrate and analysed using a linear mixed-effects model. Habitat use differed significantly between invasive and native loach species. Post-hoc comparisons and effect sizes (Hedges’ g) indicated a pronounced divergence for muddy substrate, with native Misgurnus fossilis showing substantially higher mud use than Asian weatherloaches, while differences in selection for gravel and sand were small. These findings support the adaptive flexibility hypothesis by indicating a more generalist substrate-use pattern in invasive Asian weatherloaches relative to the mud-specialised European weatherfish. From a management perspective, conserving and restoring structurally complex muddy floodplain habitats may provide a competitive refuge for European weatherfish and should be prioritised alongside targeted monitoring of Asian weatherloach spread and habitat overlap.

items.titel: A sample-to-identification workflow to monitor animal and plant biodiversity using metabarcoding and real time analysis
items.samenvatting_bron: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a transformative tool for biodiversity monitoring, offering a non-invasive means to detect and identify species across various ecosystems. However, despite its potential, current eDNA methodologies have significant limitations, including limited sensitivity, restriction to a specific taxonomic group, lengthy processing times, the need for specialized laboratory conditions and equipment, as well as computational bottlenecks in equipment, connectivity, and algorithms. Overcoming these limitations is crucial for the real-time monitoring of a high number of taxa in field-based scenarios. items.titel: Marine ecosystem ecology at a crossroads
items.samenvatting_bron: Research in marine ecosystem ecology increasingly integrates biodiversity status and trends, ecosystem functioning, and human pressures. Understanding how marine biodiversity supports ecosystem functioning remains central to the field, while growing concern over ecosystem condition has shifted attention towards relationships between human pressures and ecological responses. These established questions are increasingly complemented by the need to anticipate climate-driven ecosystem transformations and translate ecological knowledge into effective conservation and management. Resilience – the capacity of ecosystems to persist and maintain their state and functions through resistance to and recovery from disturbance – has therefore become a central scientific priority under intensifying cumulative pressures. Major challenges for the coming decade include ecological non-stationarity, rapidly expanding data volumes, erosion of traditional expertise, uneven uptake of technological advances, and restoration under changing environmental conditions. Meeting these challenges requires marine ecosystem ecology to keep pace with global change while improving the transfer of knowledge into policy and management. Here, we identify these priorities and outline pathways towards more predictive, integrated, and decision-relevant marine ecosystem science.

items.titel: Distributed Leadership for Mission Integration
items.samenvatting_bron: As Catholic and Vincentian institutions navigate increasing religious pluralism, declining numbers of vowed religious, and changing expectations about leadership, new models of mission leadership are needed. This article proposes distributed leadership for mission as a framework for sustaining Catholic and Vincentian identity in higher education. Drawing from the history of Vincent de Paul, Louise de Marillac, and the Vincentian Family, as well as contemporary scholarship on leadership and organizational effectiveness, it argues that mission is best carried forward through intentional networks of leaders who share responsibility for cultivating institutional culture and advancing a common purpose. The article explores the theoretical foundations of distributed leadership, highlights the importance of relationships, community, compassion, and ongoing formation, and identifies practices that foster mission integration across an institution of Catholic higher education. It concludes that distributed leadership reflects contemporary organizational realities, the emerging character and needs of the Catholic Church, and the deepest traditions of the Vincentian charism, offering a sustainable path for mission effectiveness in the twenty-first century.

items.titel: Circular Transformation in the Silk Sector: A Fuzzy Delphi–DEMATEL Analysis of Critical Factors
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT The circular transformation in the silk industry is crucial for enhancing resource efficiency and minimizing waste. Despite growing interest in circularity within the textile sector, the silk industry remains underexplored. This study addresses this gap by systematically assessing the barriers and enablers influencing circular economy adoption in silk. A two‐stage methodology was applied. First, a comprehensive literature review combined with expert input identified key factors, which were then validated using the fuzzy Delphi method (FDM) with 16 experts from industry and academia, resulting in nine barriers and 12 enablers. Next, the Decision‐Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) technique examined the prominence and causal relationships among these factors. Results indicate that lack of policy support from fashion brands, ineffective planning, and inadequate communication are the most significant barriers, while limited consumer awareness and high technology costs strongly influence other barriers. Key enablers include upcycling business models, rediscovery of silk knowledge, and waste material recovery. Resource efficiency culture, design for longevity, and traditional expertise act as causal drivers. The study provides actionable guidance for managers, policymakers, and researchers, offering practical and theoretical insights to advance circularity in silk.

Drawing on a panel dataset of European Union member states spanning 2009–2021, we find that progress on the Sustainable Development Goals is negatively associated with circular economy outcomes, indicating potential trade‐offs between these major sustainability initiatives. Sandwiched between the end of the Pleistocene and the emergence of agricultural lifeways, the Danish Mesolithic is characterised by marked changes in microlith design from lanceolates to geometrics and finally to transversal forms with wide front edges. These changes are synonymous with the transitions between the traditionally defined cultures of the Early, Middle and Late Mesolithic, yet the forces shaping them remain opaque. Here we present lithic, faunal, and a combination of archaeobotanical and palaeobotanical proxies, suggesting that the use of arrow poison was a likely driver for microlithic design change. An analysis of ballistically relevant morphometric attributes of lithics found in direct association with hunted prey suggests that the use of poison was prevalent during the Early Mesolithic when targeted game animals were also largest. Thereafter, lithic projectile points became larger and game animals smaller, likely reflecting Holocene faunal downsizing alongside changing hunting strategies. Palaeobotanical evidence from Denmark and southern Sweden suggests that a wide range of toxic plants were available throughout the Holocene. items.titel: A Call for Systematic Integration of Family‐Focused Care in Clinical Nursing Practice in Europe: A Position Paper
items.samenvatting_bron: AIM: To highlight the need for a shift to family-focused care and to outline how this transition should be developed and implemented through close collaboration between clinical practice and research. DESIGN: Position paper. METHOD: Members of Family Health in Europe-Research in Nursing (FAME-RN) developed the position paper through an iterative process informed by selected literature, established care models and collective expertise in family nursing. The paper examines distinctions between patient-centred, person-centred, family-centred and family-focused care and considers key barriers, enablers and priorities for implementation across European healthcare settings. RESULTS: Family-focused care recognises families as essential partners in caring for individuals with severe or chronic conditions across the lifespan, working with families as interconnected systems and as an explicit unit of nursing assessment and intervention rather than solely involving them as individuals in care. The position paper identifies key priorities for implementation including conceptual clarity, systematic family assessment, family-level interventions, education and competence development, organisational leadership, supportive policy, co-design with families and implementation-focused research. CONCLUSION: Ensuring that families have access to appropriate information, support and resources enhances caregiving capacity while protecting family health and well-being. items.titel: Strategising social innovation paradoxes: four faces of energy citizenship
items.samenvatting_bron: Social innovation (SI) is an increasingly prominent area of innovation. Involving changes in social relations, SI practice is pervaded with tensions and apparent paradoxes, however. The ‘productive use of paradox’ has been articulated theoretically and demonstrated empirically, but much remains to be elaborated in terms of SI strategies. This contribution explores the SI paradoxes from a paradox management angle. Striving for conceptual insight with empirical concreteness, the analysis invokes the example of energy citizenship. Defined as a shift from passive consumerism towards active political engagement with energy systems, it harbours several tensions. Building on empirical investigations in Belgium, we discuss and strategise four contrasting manifestations of energy citizenship. This empirical diversity helps to showcase paradoxes pertaining to citizenship, intermediation, institutionalisation and materiality. The analysis combines insights from social innovation scholarship, critical innovation studies and governance research to situate these paradoxes in wider SI discussions. Comparing paradox-handling strategies within and across energy citizenship examples, we unpack and nuance the idea of paradoxes as the ‘working substance’ of social innovation. items.titel: Opnieuw eenrichtingsverkeer voor scheepvaart op IJssel door lage waterstand
items.samenvatting_bron: De scheepvaart op de IJssel tussen de IJsselkop en Zutphen mag sinds vanochtend opnieuw maar in één richting varen. Rijkswaterstaat heeft de maatregel opnieuw ingesteld vanwege de lage waterstand. Schepen moeten daardoor weer zo'n 300 kilometer omvaren. Maandag werd het eenrichtingsverkeer nog opgeheven , omdat de minimaal gepeilde diepte op de Boven-IJssel de vereiste 1,45 meter had bereikt. Doordat er minder regen is gevallen dan verwacht, is de waterstand weer onder die grens gedaald, meldt Rijkswaterstaat. De binnenvaart mag nu alleen stroomopwaarts varen. Schepen die vanuit Duitsland de IJssel op willen, kunnen daardoor niet bij Arnhem richting Zutphen varen. Ze moeten omvaren via Amsterdam en het IJsselmeer. Het eenrichtingsverkeer heeft ook gevolgen voor de binnenvaart richting het Twentekanaal, schrijft RTV Oost . Schippers kunnen niet meer vanuit beide richtingen rechtstreeks naar het kanaal varen en moeten dus omvaren. Waterstand blijft dalen Rijkswaterstaat verwacht dat de waterstand de komende vijf dagen verder daalt. Dat hangt onder meer af van de hoeveelheid water die via de Rijn bij Lobith Nederland binnenkomt. Regen in Duitsland en Zwitserland kan ervoor zorgen dat de waterstanden weer stijgen. De waterstanden worden daarom nauwlettend in de gaten gehouden. Als die veranderen, kunnen ook de maatregelen voor de scheepvaart worden aangepast.

items.titel: Machine learning-based prediction of critical load events in airborne wind energy systems
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract. Predicting and avoiding critical load events is crucial for the reliable autonomous operation of airborne wind energy (AWE) systems. Such events can lead to actuator saturation, loss of steering authority, and increased structural stresses, eventually resulting in long-term degradation of the kite, tether, and ground-station components. The present study explores a data-driven approach to predicting tether force peaks, defined as instances in which the force exceeds a threshold set by the winch controller. The method is developed using a large-scale SCADA dataset from Kitepower's leading-edge inflatable V9 kite, including more than 1000 pumping cycles spanning 26 h of kite operation and covering a wide range of wind and operating conditions. Tether force peaks are detected and used to extract pre-peak time windows that capture the system behavior before each threshold exceedance. From these windows, statistical, temporal, and spectral features are computed from multiple kite, tether, and ground-station measurements. A supervised classification model is trained to distinguish normal operation from pre-peak dynamics. The proposed approach predicts critical load events 1 s in advance and shows strong generalization capability on flight data that was not used for training the model, correctly identifying 85.4 % of the critical load events (recall) and achieving a 90.9 % F1-score, a metric that indicates a strong balance between correctly detected events and false alarms

items.titel: From fragmented knowledge to scalable wetland restoration in Europe: The Restore4Life Integrated Wetland Reconstruction Accelerator
items.samenvatting_bron: Europe’s commitment to restore degraded ecosystems has created an urgent need to move from isolated restoration projects towards approaches that can be replicated and scaled. Wetland restoration, however, remains constrained by fragmented knowledge, incompatible datasets, inconsistent monitoring, limited transfer of experience between sites, weak stakeholder participation and insufficient links between ecological planning and long-term financing. Restore4Life addresses these barriers through an Integrated Wetland Reconstruction Accelerator that connects scientific evidence, digital decision support, field implementation, participation and finance throughout the restoration cycle. Within this framework, reconstruction refers to the active re-establishment of wetland structures, processes and functions where passive recovery alone is insufficient. The Accelerator provides a common operational framework for identifying restoration opportunities, establishing ecological baselines, selecting indicators, designing interventions, monitoring outcomes and comparing restoration trajectories. These approaches are being tested across contrasting freshwater, floodplain, deltaic and coastal demonstration sites and translated into harmonised protocols, transferable solutions and practical implementation roadmaps. items.titel: Employing environmental DNA to evaluate invasive species removal and spatiotemporal dynamics of pupfish, crayfish, and Green Sunfish in a desert spring system
items.samenvatting_bron: Aquatic invasive species disrupt ecosystem function and threaten native biodiversity through predation, competition, and habitat alteration. Eradication offers the best chance for ecosystem recovery but requires substantial time and resources, and detection of invasives at low densities is challenging. Environmental DNA (eDNA) sampling of genetic material shed by organisms into the environment provides a sensitive, cost-effective, and noninvasive alternative to traditional detection methods. In this study, we applied eDNA methods to inform invasive species eradication at Ash Meadows National Wildlife Refuge and explore spatiotemporal dynamics of endangered Ash Meadows Amargosa Pupfish (Cyprinodon nevadensis mionectes), and invasive Green Sunfish (Lepomis cyanellus), and Red Swamp Crayfish (Procambarus clarkii) in the target warm spring system. First, we quantified eDNA transport using a caged Green Sunfish experiment, then used these results to inform repeated eDNA sampling alongside traditional capture methods (gill nets, trap nets, electrofishing) to determine Green Sunfish distribution, target removal efforts, and evaluate eradication. Modeling indicated that collection of one sample every 160 m yielded >0.95 detection probability for 3 fish, while collection of 10 samples was required to reach the same detection probability for 1 fish (95% CI: 2–57). items.titel: Onderzoek naar een nieuwe, op DNA gebaseerde selectiemethode voor het identificeren van genclusters voor de biosynthese van antibiotica
items.samenvatting_bron: Antibiotics are indispensable for modern medicine as they allow the treatment of infectious diseases and enable invasive medical procedures. However, their incorrect and widespread use has caused an increase in antibiotic resistance, making the discovery of novel antibiotics urgent. Most antibiotics in clinical use are derived from micro-organisms. Unfortunately, traditional techniques suffer from the limited culturability and sensitivity needed to detect antibiotic-producing organisms, resulting in the discovery of only the "low hanging fruit" of antibiotic candidates. Accessing the large potential known to be still present in nature therefore requires new approaches to circumvent these limitations and expand the repertoire of antibiotics known today. In this work, we aimed to set the first steps towards a novel approach, using a polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based droplet-platform to adopt a genotype-based, culture-independent method with increased throughput and sensitivity. A PCR-assay with newly developed degenerate primers will be used to enrich gene cluster types of interest. Combined with high-throughput screening of large metagenomic libraries, built with environmental DNA (eDNA), and functional characterization of recovered clones, we anticipate that this approach will enable the detection of a larger diversity of antibiotics and complement current detection methodologies.

items.titel: Coastal benthic ecosystems in a changing ocean: a mini review
items.samenvatting_bron: Coastal benthic ecosystems are shaped by the combined effects of climate change and anthropogenic pressures. Ocean warming, acidification, and deoxygenation interact with eutrophication, pollution, bottom trawling, and coastal development, altering biodiversity, habitat structure, and functioning from shallow coasts to continental margins. Benthic communities, comprising infaunal and epifaunal taxa, regulate key processes including nutrient cycling, sediment dynamics, and carbon burial, thereby underpinning benthic-pelagic coupling and biogeochemical dynamics. Rising temperatures and marine heatwaves drive widespread losses of habitat-forming species, while ocean acidification constrains calcification. Warming, acidification, hypoxia, eutrophication, and pollution increasingly simplify assemblages, and alter trophic pathways and performance. Interactions among stressors can amplify organismal sensitivity and push ecosystems towards ecological thresholds. However, many knowledge gaps remain. Recent methodological advances, including environmental DNA metabarcoding, automated imaging, trait-based analyses, and multi-stressor experiments, are improving the detection of ecosystem changes at large and our mechanistic understanding of ecosystem responses to ongoing change. items.titel: Simple soil eDNA sampling reveals terrestrial mammal diversity in the Central Kalahari and highlights waterholes as sampling hotspots
items.samenvatting_bron: Remote and vast ecosystems present a challenge for biodiversity monitoring. The Central Kalahari Game Reserve in Botswana is one such ecosystem spanning 52,800 km2, a mosaic of fossilized rivers, clay pans, semi-arid sand dunes, scrub, and woodland. It is one of the last remaining untouched wildernesses in the world and hosts unique biodiversity, including populations of threatened mammals. Due to its extreme arid environment, size, and inaccessibility, surveying biodiversity across the reserve is both logistically and technically difficult. Here we demonstrate that a low-effort approach of sampling soil across the reserve is an efficient way to rapidly assess the terrestrial mammal biodiversity using eDNA metabarcoding. We found that eDNA from soil near waterholes performed better at capturing local biodiversity than soil from roads. eDNA metabarcoding detected 38 mammal species, 15 bird species and two amphibians and a simultaneously conducted camera trapping study detected 29 mammal species. eDNA was particularly powerful for detecting small-bodied taxa, including murids, mongooses and bats, which were largely missed by camera traps, while camera trapping was aimed at and performed well for detecting felids. items.titel: Community-Driven Fisheries Innovations for Climate Adaptation and a Sustainable Blue Economy
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Small-scale fisheries are among the most climate-vulnerable socio-ecological systems, facing threats from rising sea temperatures, ocean acidification, extreme weather, and shifting species distributions. Yet, they are also dynamic sites of innovation where communities develop adaptive solutions. Drawing on a non-systematic review of literature from 2016–2025, this article synthesizes community-led innovations across Africa, Asia, Oceania, Europe, and Latin America and examines how local ecological knowledge, co-management, and technological practices converge to strengthen resilience. Across regions, empowerment emerges as both a mechanism and an outcome: women’s cooperatives in Nigeria and Mexico increased household security, youth-driven digital platforms in Ecuador and Hawaii built adaptive capacity, and Indigenous stewardship in North America safeguarded both biodiversity and cultural continuity. Scaling these innovations requires supportive governance, access to finance, and protections for local agencies. Far from being marginal, community-driven fisheries innovations are central to climate adaptation and must be recognized as core strategies for building a sustainable blue economy.
