items.titel: On the scaling-up of 3D-printed metallic POCS structured catalysts membrane reactors
items.samenvatting_bron: This work reports the first experimental demonstration of a scaled-up multi-membrane reactor for ammonia synthesis, integrating four tubular carbon molecular sieve membranes (CMSMs) with two 3D-printed metallic Periodic Open Cellular Structure (POCS) supports of Gyroid and Body-Centred Cubic (BCC) geometry, manufactured in Inconel 625 by Laser Powder Bed Fusion and washcoated with a Ru-based catalyst via a scaled-up dip-spin coating procedure. The coating protocol transferred to both topologies at the larger scale without modification, with optical microscopy confirming uniform, crack-free coverage.. Novolac-based CMSM carbonized at 550 °C were characterised by organic elemental analysis, XPS, and Raman spectroscopy, confirming a defect-rich, turbostratic sp 2 carbon matrix with microporous architecture. Baseline testing in the conventional reactor over 350–450 °C and 20–40 bar(g) demonstrated that Gyroid and BCC configurations deliver virtually identical catalytic performance, reflecting the dominance of reaction kinetics and thermodynamics over geometry-dependent transport resistances. Upon membrane integration, this geometry-independence was preserved, and the membrane consistently enhanced NH 3 production rates across all operating conditions. items.titel: Neighbourhood Built Environment and Sense of Community in Tropical Residential Neighbourhoods: An Observation-Based Comparative Study in Malaysia
items.samenvatting_bron: The neighbourhood-built environment plays an important role in shaping social interaction and the development of a sense of community, particularly in rapidly urbanising tropical cities. While previous Malaysian studies have primarily used perception-based surveys, limited empirical attention has been given to the actual observation of physical neighbourhood features and their influence on social interaction and community cohesion. This study uses an observational analysis of two master-planned townships in Shah Alam, Selangor: Setia Alam and Bukit Jelutong, to evaluate the link between neighbourhood-built environment characteristics and a sense of community. A structured observation protocol was employed to assess eleven neighbourhoodbuilt environment attributes, including residential density, green infrastructure, architectural style, and recreational facilities, using a three point assessment scale. The findings indicate that although both neighbourhoods possess physical characteristics that support community development, they achieve these outcomes through different spatial planning approaches. Setia Alam scores in architectural, housing design excellence, and strong urban integration, promoting community identity and social interactions. Bukit Jelutong, on the other hand, benefits from lowered density, greater block sizes, and large green networks, which enhance spatial comfort and spontaneous social connections. items.titel: Lisbon
items.samenvatting_bron: This chapter examines how Lisbon’s climate‑neutrality agenda intersects with long‑standing socio‑spatial inequalities, housing precarity, and contested urban development paths. It reconstructs the historical and demographic trajectories that have shaped the Portuguese capital, highlighting the legacies of colonialism, touristification, and financialisation in producing uneven access to housing, mobility, and energy‑efficient dwellings. The chapter analyses the evolution of Lisbon’s climate governance architecture, from early commitments under the Covenant of Mayors to the Climate Action Plan 2030 and participation in the European Union’s mission for climate‑neutral and smart cities, focusing on the role of municipal departments, the energy and environment agency Lisboa E‑Nova, and an expanding ecosystem of open‑data platforms. It then explores how specific policies and projects in mobility, green infrastructure, water management, energy retrofitting, and the circular economy translate strategic visions into experiments on the ground, while also generating new distributive and procedural dilemmas. Particular attention is paid to forms of citizen participation and climate activism, including participatory budgeting, citizens’ assemblies, and climate‑justice movements, and to their ambivalent relationship with institutional initiatives.

items.titel: Construction of Dynamic Ecological Networks in Large-Scale Open-Pit Mining Areas on the Loess Plateau
items.samenvatting_bron: The Loess Plateau is a typical ecologically fragile area, where long-term intensive open-pit mining triggers severe vegetation loss, habitat fragmentation, and biodiversity decline. Although ecological network analysis integrating circuit theory and complex-network topology has become a mainstream connectivity assessment tool, existing studies mainly focus on urban agglomerations, nature reserves, and mountainous regions. Long-term dynamic networks considering mining and reclamation remain insufficiently understood in large coalfields. Taking the Pingshuo mining area as a case, this study combined MSPA, the MCR model, circuit theory, and complex-network approaches using remote-sensing images (1985, 1995, 2005, 2015, 2025), DEM, and road data to analyze 41-year spatiotemporal changes and propose a 2025 optimization plan. Ecological source proportion dropped from 6.17% (1985) to 3.56% (2015), then recovered to 9.79% (2025), dominated by forests and grasslands. Corridor length declined from 150.90 km to 99.32 km, and the 2025 network showed an average degree of 1.82 and an average path length of 1.45, indicating fragility. Under the proposed optimization scenario, node connectivity and network stability were projected to improve substantially. This study reveals how mining and restoration jointly shape ecological networks, offering a model-based theoretical framework for ecological security planning in similar fragile mining regions.

items.titel: Newly planted woodlands improve connectivity for woodland fauna, flora and fungi
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Context Young planted woodlands may only support a small proportion of the biodiversity found in mature woodlands but may play an important role in promoting species movements and enhancing biodiversity due to their emerging structural similarities. Objectives We assessed whether recently planted woodlands increase connectivity between mature woodland patches relative to agricultural fields, and whether responses vary across active (small mammals, ground invertebrates) and passive (plants, fungi) dispersers. Methods We used a multi-taxa natural experiment across paired sites where mature woodlands were either connected by planted woodland or separated by farmland. Movement was quantified using PIT-tagging of small mammals and beetles, pitfall trapping, vegetation surveys, airborne spore traps and soil eDNA metabarcoding. A Bayesian beta-binomial model estimated taxon-specific habitat preferences for dispersal. Results Although we did not detect inter-patch movements, we detected higher movement of wood mice, ground active invertebrates, plants, and fungi into new woodlands relative to agricultural fields, whereas, field voles exhibited minimal movement, and some airborne fungal groups showed reduced movement within planted woodlands. items.titel: Estimating absolute DNA abundance from replicated metabarcoding
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Datasets derived from mixed‐template DNA amplification and sequencing (‘metabarcoding’) are common in environmental DNA (eDNA), microbiome or microbial ecology analyses. Such metabarcoding data have been broadly used to inform estimates of biodiversity, distribution and abundance across a wide range of species and habitats. Generally, data from metabarcoding consist of a table of read‐counts assigned to each of a set of taxa or sequence variants. As such, they appear to contain quantitative information about the environment under study, immediately eligible for traditional community ecology analyses. In fact, metabarcoding data are compositional, can be biased by variation in PCR amplification rates among taxa, and have other statistical attributes that are distinct from many other common ecological observations. The difficulty in understanding and accounting for the complexity of metabarcoding observations has hindered their ecological interpretation and limited their integration with other ecological data types. Here, we use both simulations and empirical observations to show that the variability among replicate metabarcoding observations is closely tied to the absolute quantities of DNA present in a sample. We then develop a general statistical model for estimating DNA abundance from metabarcoding observations using the relationship between mean and variance of metabarcoding reads. items.titel: Operational comparability of ecological status assessment in Iberian transboundary rivers
items.samenvatting_bron: The European Union Water Framework Directive (WFD) requires member states to assess the ecological status of surface waters using biological quality elements (BQEs). Although the WFD includes intercalibration procedures to harmonise class boundaries, differences between national assessment systems may affect the comparability of ecological status classifications, particularly in transboundary rivers. This study evaluated the consistency of Portuguese and Spanish ecological status assessments in 32 water bodies across Iberian transboundary rivers in the Minho, Lima, Douro, Tagus and Guadiana basins, using data collected between 2019 and 2021. Comparisons included fish, macrophytes, benthic macroinvertebrates and diatoms. Biological assemblages, ecological quality ratios (EQRs) and ecological quality classifications were analysed. Results differed markedly among BQEs. Fish showed no significant differences in assemblage composition or EQR values between countries and a moderate positive correlation in ecological quality classifications. Macroinvertebrates displayed weak compositional separation, no differences in EQR values and a weak, nonsignificant positive correlation between countries. Macrophytes showed significant compositional differences despite similar EQR distributions and a weak, nonsignificant positive correlation in ecological quality classifications. items.titel: Synthesizing lessons from European adaptation pathways projects for climate resilience
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate adaptation planning faces challenges due to deep uncertainty and complex socio-ecological systems, often resulting in fragmented and incremental responses. This study synthesizes experiences from 21 cities and regions across eight European Union-funded projects, employing diverse methodologies to develop adaptation pathways that sequence climate adaptation measures over time. Through a systematic approach answering research questions across 8 themes to reveal lessons learned, we find varied stakeholder engagement approaches, data limitations influencing pathway quantification, inconsistent use of adaptation tipping points, and challenges integrating pathways with spatial and urban planning frameworks. While adaptation pathways enhance long-term strategic thinking and stakeholder collaboration, their institutional embedding and operationalization remain challenging within projects. Two main directions for future pathways research and practice are derived: (1) Embedding adaptation-pathway thinking into governance and planning; and (2) Addressing data needs, robust monitoring and multidimensional uncertainties. The study underscores the importance of flexible, inclusive, and data-informed approaches to support dynamic adaptation under uncertainty. items.titel: Diminishing cooling returns of urban greening amid a warming climate
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban greening is widely prioritized as a nature-based solution to mitigating intensifying heat extremes in the context of climate change, yet its long-term global efficacy remains inadequately quantified. Here we present a two-decade assessment of vegetation dynamics and associated cooling effects across 3,806 urban clusters worldwide, integrating multisource satellite observations with ground measurements from 4,855 meteorological stations. We identify a pronounced climate equity gap: While cities in the Global North have largely expanded green infrastructure, they exhibit cooling saturation with diminishing biophysical returns. Conversely, most cities in the Global South show vegetation stagnation or loss, compounding rapid warming trends. This asymmetry exposes a critical climate justice challenge, indicating that current greening efforts are insufficient to offset a warming trend. Our findings underscore the necessity for context-specific, integrated climate adaptation frameworks that address both the quantity and quality of urban vegetation to achieve equitable thermal resilience in an increasingly warm world.

items.titel: Hydraulic Modelling and Traditional Water Management for Nature-Based Flood Adaptation: A Spatial Planning Framework in the Lower Segura Basin (SE Spain)
items.samenvatting_bron: Flood adaptation in Mediterranean river basins requires approaches addressing floodwater circulation, redistribution and accumulation. This study proposes an exploratory spatial planning framework integrating two-dimensional hydraulic modelling, official flood hazard mapping and traditional water-management knowledge to identify potential Nature-based Solutions (NbS). Applied to the lower Segura basin (southeastern Spain), HEC-RAS 6.6 simulations used spatially uniform extreme rainfall to analyse water depths, velocities and the depth–velocity index (h·v). Functional hydraulic corridors were delineated using a threshold of h·v ≥ 0.30 m2/s. Comparison of simulated inundation with official SNCZI T500 mapping revealed 106.11 km2 of overlap (31.59%:, 182.42 km2 identified exclusively by the model (54.31%) and 47.34 km2 identified exclusively by SNCZI (14.09%). Qualitative spatial correspondence with traditional boquera irrigation systems and azarbe drainage networks informed a preliminary green infrastructure proposal combining multifunctional corridors, drainage adaptations and Controlled Storage Areas. The framework demonstrates the potential of integrating hydraulic modelling and historical knowledge into territorial flood adaptation planning. However, the simulations were not independently validated, and the hydraulic effectiveness of the proposed NbS remains unquantified.

items.titel: Bilbao
items.samenvatting_bron: This chapter analyses Bilbao as a paradigmatic case of urban climate governance in a post‑industrial European city. It first traces the city’s historical trajectory from industrial hub to culture‑led regeneration “model”, highlighting how Bilbao Ría 2000, the Guggenheim Museum, and large infrastructure projects reshaped the Nervión estuary and re-positioned the city within global urban networks. It then situates Bilbao’s climate policies within the multi-level Basque and Spanish framework, examining the interplay between KLIMA 2050; the Basque Energy Strategy 2030; the urban agenda Bultzatu 2050; and municipal instruments such as the Environmental Strategy 2020–2050, the Adaptation Plan, and the PACES 2030 climate and energy action plan. items.titel: ECOLOGICAL CHALLENGES AND CLIMATE CHANGE IN TÜRKİYE: RISKS, SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AND ADAPTATION STRATEGIES
items.samenvatting_bron: This article examines the principal environmental challenges facing Türkiye in the context of climate change and considers policy options for strengthening ecological security and sustainable development. Based on a qualitative review of international assessments and national climate policy documents, the study analyses water stress, drought, extreme heat, wildfires, floods, coastal risks, biodiversity loss and greenhouse-gas emissions. It discusses the relationship between climate vulnerability and economic sectors, particularly energy, agriculture, urban infrastructure and tourism. The analysis highlights the importance of combining mitigation measures with adaptation planning, including renewable energy, energy efficiency, integrated water management, climate-resilient agriculture, early-warning systems and nature-based solutions. Türkiye's 2024–2030 climate mitigation and adaptation plans provide an institutional framework, while implementation depends on coordination among national and local authorities, businesses and communities. The article concludes that an integrated, evidence-based approach can reduce climate risks while supporting economic resilience and a fair green transition.

items.titel: Coupled ecological pressures in urban environments: regional heterogeneity and drivers of carbon and water footprints
items.samenvatting_bron: A synergistic assessment of carbon and water footprints is essential for capturing the complexity of compound ecological pressures in rapidly urbanizing cities. However, their spatial distributions and integrated mechanisms at the district scale remain insufficiently explored and quantified. This study develops a spatially explicit analytical framework that integrates carbon and three types of water footprints (on-site blue water, runoff blue water, and road runoff gray water) with spatial autocorrelation and the Optimal Parameters-based Geographical Detector (OPGD) method. The analysis focuses on six central districts in Guangzhou, China, and evaluates spatial clustering patterns alongside the joint effects of natural and human drivers. The results reveal significant intra-urban clustering and a distinct core–periphery gradient in ecological footprints. This pattern is shaped primarily by urbanization intensity, human activities, and natural features, and interactions among these drivers generate marked nonlinear amplification. Consequently, ecological burdens are concentrated in densely populated and intensively developed districts, exacerbating spatial inequality and exposing specific areas to elevated environmental risks. The convergence of high urbanization levels with overlapping ecological pressures underscores the urgency of targeted urban sustainability strategies. document.tekst_begin: De beweging naar een sterkere eerste lijn 2-meting ten behoeve van monitoring van het Integraal Zorgakkoord Ilgin Arslan Lisa Jansen Marloes Meijer Claudia Laarman Julia Simanowski Lilian van Tuyl Het Nivel levert kennis om de gezondheidszorg in Nederland beter te maken. Dat doen we met hoogwaardig, betrouwbaar en onafhankelijk wetenschappelijk onderzoek naar thema’s met een groot maatschappelijk belang. ‘Kennis voor betere zorg’ is onze missie. Met onze kennis dragen we bij aan het continu verbeteren en vernieuwen van de gezondheidszorg. We vinden het belangrijk dat mensen in staat zijn om deel te nemen aan de samenleving. Ons onderzoek draait uiteindelijk om de vraag hoe we de zorg voor de patiënt kunnen verbeteren. Alle onderzoeken publiceert het Nivel openbaar, dat is statutair vastgelegd. Doel van het toezicht was om te bepalen of Jeugdzorg verantwoorde vrijwillige ambulante jeugdzorg en jeugdbescherming verleent. document.tekst_begin: Position paper Rondetafelgesprek Algemene Maatregel van Bestuur (AMvB) Dierwaardige veehouderij Prof. Dr. Saskia S. Arndt, Hoogleraar Diergedrag Universiteit Utrecht, faculteit Diergeneeskunde Innovatie in de veehouderij vraagt ook om innovatie op het terrein van dierenwelzijn De zes leidende principes zoals die in 2021 door de Raad voor Dierenaangelegenheden (RDA) zijn geformuleerd, vormen samen een normatief en praktisch kader voor een dierwaardige veehouderij. Ze sluiten inhoudelijk aan bij het Five Domains Model van Mellor et al. (1994, 2015, 2016, 2020), dat aandacht besteedt aan voeding, leefomgeving, gezondheid, gedrag en de daaruit voortkomende mentale ervaringen van dieren. De RDA voegt daaraan een expliciet ethisch uitgangspunt toe: erkenning van de intrinsieke waarde en integriteit van het dier. Dit uitgangspunt bepaalt mede hoe mensen hun omgang met dieren behoren in te richten. Dierwaardigheid en dierenwelzijn hangen nauw samen. Binnen de dynamische benadering van dierenwelzijn kan (positief) welzijn worden beschreven aan hand van het vermogen van een dier om mentaal en fysiek adequaat te reageren op positieve en negatieve prikkels uit zijn interne en externe omgeving.

document.tekst_begin: 22.10.2026 Position paper Eyes on Animals: Neem de wettelijke opdracht als het toetsingskader voor de AMvB 1. Voorziet de ontwerp-AMvB in het borgen van het doel van de wet en het uitwerken van de inhoudelijke criteria? Met het gewijzigde amendement-De Groot/Van Campen (35 746, nr. 30) heeft de Tweede Kamer een wettelijke opdracht vastgelegd: bij AMvB moeten regels worden gesteld die gericht zijn op het uiterlijk in 2040 bewerkstelligen van een dierwaardige veehouderij. De Raad van State heeft in 2023 aangegeven dat het doel van de wet in de uitwerking overeind moet blijven staan. De wetgever heeft daarbij expliciete inhoudelijke criteria opgenomen: een dierwaardige veehouderij moet voorzien in respect voor de intrinsieke waarde en integriteit van dieren, goede voeding, een goede omgeving, goede gezondheid en natuurlijk gedrag. Ook moeten regels worden gesteld over het beëindigen van bepaalde lichamelijke ingrepen en moeten de criteria leiden tot een overwegend positieve emotionele toestand van het dier. items.titel: Cave Monitoring Network and Long-Term Ecological Research in Portugal
items.samenvatting_bron: This document describes the Portuguese Cave Monitoring Network (CaveNet), a scientific infrastructure established within the framework of the EcoSub Chair. CaveNet provides an integrated framework for the quantitative monitoring of caves in Portugal, encompassing data collection, validation, processing and storage. The document presents the architecture and objectives of the infrastructure, highlights its scientific and ecological relevance and characterises the sites selected for Long-Term Ecological Research in Portuguese caves (LTER-Grutas). These sites host monitoring stations whose long-term environmental and ecological data are integrated into CaveNet. The document further discusses the advantages of an integrated cave monitoring network and its direct applicability to the assessment and reporting of the conservation status of habitat type 8310 - Caves not open to the public - under the Natura 2000 framework, as well as to the implementation of the Nature Restoration Regulation. In addition, CaveNet has significant socio-economic value, particularly in supporting the assessment and management of occupational risks associated with exposure to environmental hazards during underground work. In the longer term, the infrastructure will enable innovative research on carbon fluxes across the atmosphere–soil–subsoil–groundwater continuum, subsurface radioactivity emissions and the implications of subterranean processes for ecosystem services. items.titel: Sustainable development practices and SDG integration in brownfield redevelopment
items.samenvatting_bron: This chapter examines how sustainable development principles and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) can be systematically integrated into brownfield redevelopment to transform derelict and contaminated land into socially inclusive, environmentally restored, and economically productive urban assets. Drawing on the triple bottom line framework of environmental repair, economic viability, and social well-being, the chapter demonstrates how brownfield reuse inherently advances multiple SDGs simultaneously from improved public health and clean water to climate action, decent work, and sustainable cities. It reviews the international, European, and UK policy frameworks that drive sustainable brownfield practice, including the EU Green Deal, the National Planning Policy Framework, and associated funding mechanisms. Innovative and eco-friendly remediation techniques spanning bioremediation, phytoremediation, in-situ chemical treatment, nature-based solutions, and circular material reuse are evaluated for their sustainability credentials. The chapter further addresses adaptive reuse of existing structures, climate-resilient design, green infrastructure integration, and the social imperatives of community engagement, affordable housing, economic inclusion, and environmental justice. items.titel: Does the climate-adaptive city pilot policy exacerbate urban sprawl? Evidence from a quasi-natural experiment in China
items.samenvatting_bron: Although climate-adaptive policies are primarily designed to enhance urban resilience, they may also generate unintended consequences for urban spatial development. However, the impacts of climate-adaptive governance interventions on urban sprawl remain underexplored. This study employs double machine learning method to examine how the climate-adaptive urban pilot policy affects urban sprawl and the underlying mechanisms, using 285 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2010 to 2021. Results show that pilot policy significantly promotes urban sprawl, a conclusion validated by robustness tests. Fiscal resource allocation and green infrastructure expansion are plausible potential pathways behind this effect, while land use efficiency and intensity show no significant impact. Noticeable heterogeneity exists across city characteristics; the policy generates a stronger sprawl effect in non-central cities than in central cities, and its impacts increase with city size. Along the urbanization gradient, the policy effect follows a U-shaped pattern and is most prominent in highly urbanized areas. Moreover, suggestive evidence points to policy-related spillovers from climate-adaptive pilot contributing to urban sprawl in adjacent regions. items.samenvatting_bron: This article aims to examine and propose development approaches for Bangkok’s recreation business sector in 2026 within the context of contemporary urban development that emphasizes quality of urban life, the creative economy, and the experience economy. The study employs a literature review and conceptual analysis based on Urban Recreation, Leisure Studies, and Quality of Urban Life, integrated with the experience economy framework, to explain the role of recreation businesses in large metropolitan cities. The findings indicate that recreation businesses play a significant role in enhancing urban well-being, social interaction, and city livability, particularly in high-density urban contexts such as Bangkok. Appropriate development approaches include the provision of personalized recreation activities, investment in experience-based technologies, lifestyle-oriented marketing through micro-influencer strategies, and the development of recreation communities to support long-term business sustainability. In addition, policy-level recommendations are proposed, including the expansion of urban green spaces, support for creative businesses, and the promotion of creative districts. The study highlights that integrating economic, experiential, technological, and urban planning dimensions is essential for strengthening the competitiveness of Bangkok’s recreation business sector and supporting sustainable urban development in the long term.

items.titel: Why Do Goitered Gazelles Cross the Path of an Approaching Moving Object Instead of Fleeing?
items.samenvatting_bron: Animal–vehicle collisions are an important conservation concern. Although many studies examine road mortality and wildlife crossings, less is known about ungulates that run across the path of an approaching vehicle rather than simply fleeing. This study describes this behavior in goitered gazelles (Gazella subgutturosa) and examines its association with four recorded factors: approach category, group size, group composition, and month. In a forward stepwise logistic regression, approach category was associated with crossing behavior (Wald = 22.784, df = 2, p < 0.001). The odds of crossing were higher in the high-category group than in the low-category group (odds ratio = 2.36). However, the categories also differed in object type (cars, motor scooters, and bicycles/pedestrians), so the independent effect of speed cannot be separated from the effect of object type. Group size, group composition, and month did not meet the model’s entry criteria. These observational results identify an association, but do not determine whether path-crossing is a uniquely anti-predator response, a reaction to limited assessment time, or another form of behavior.

items.titel: On-site metabarcoding analysis of environmental DNA samples
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Environmental DNA metabarcoding is a powerful monitoring tool for assessing aquatic biodiversity, as well as the sustainability and impacts of fisheries and aquaculture. However, conventional laboratory workflows remain time-consuming and dependent on dedicated infrastructures. Here, we present a field trial of a fully portable, off-site eDNA metabarcoding pipeline that enables end-to-end analysis within a few days using compact equipment, including a BentoLab workstation and an Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) MinION sequencer. The workflow was implemented during two international training courses in Norway and Brazil, where students and early career researchers collected environmental samples, extracted and amplified DNA, prepared DNA libraries, and sequenced on-site before performing bioinformatics and statistical analyses. In the case study detailed here, seven eDNA samples collected and analysed on-site in the Oslofjord allowed detection of 16 fish and elasmobranch species. Although overall diversity was lower than in earlier studies using Illumina-based sequencing, our protocol reliably detected key species and demonstrates that portable eDNA metabarcoding is feasible for rapid ecological assessment, surveillance of high-risk regions and/or deployment in remote or resource-limited settings.

items.titel: Persistence of sedimentary DNA in burrowing marine benthos: evidence from the decapod Upogebia major

Requiring only small environmental samples, eDNA analysis enables efficient assessment of the occurrence and distribution of target taxa based on eDNA detection and concentration. This approach is particularly effective for organisms difficult to observe and collect conventionally. However, knowledge of eDNA persistence in the environment remains limited. A better understanding of taxon-specific eDNA persistence is essential for accurate interpretation of eDNA data. Burrowing benthic organisms are suitable targets for eDNA-based surveys because they are difficult to collect and observe directly, making field surveys time-consuming and labor-intensive. However, little is known about the persistence of their eDNA. items.titel: Biogeographical context mediates land-use impacts on tropical soil multitrophic diversity
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract 1. Soil communities are structured primarily by climate, soil properties and regional biogeographic history. In addition, land-use change is expected to reorganise soil multitrophic diversity in a predictable direction: by raising resource availability and disturbance, forest-to-pasture conversion should shift multitrophic communities from slow-growing organisms, dominated by fungi and large-bodied consumers, towards fast-growing ones, dominated by bacteria and small-bodied consumers. This prediction has been tested in temperate systems, where biogeographic and environmental heterogeneity is very different from the tropics. items.titel: Waterborne eDNA metabarcoding of the upper Llano River watershed (Texas, USA) detects regionally unreported green plant taxa
items.samenvatting_bron: Environmental DNA (eDNA) represents a promising preliminary tool for efficiently assessing biological diversity in locales where conducting intensive field surveys is logistically challenging, as in the case of west-central Texas. Its utility for characterizing biodiversity across broad spatial scales is amplified in lotic systems, which can transport eDNA several kilometers from its source and often contain signals from both aquatic and nearby terrestrial organisms. In the present study, we employed waterborne eDNA metabarcoding to broadly characterize regional green plant (Viridiplantae) diversity in two west-central Texas rivers, the North Llano River and the South Llano River, that constitute the upper reaches of the ecologically and economically important Llano River watershed. We detected taxa from 45 green plant families, encompassing both streptophytes and chlorophytes. Among these, 18 taxa had not been previously documented in the study area, representing putative novel distributional data pending direct field observations. Additionally, we assessed the influence of three methodological factors—sequencing depth, PCR template volume, and volume of water filtered—on detected diversity. Collectively, our findings highlight the value and limitations of eDNA metabarcoding for broad-scale biodiversity characterization and provide insights into the potentially unrecognized floristic diversity of understudied Texas rivers.

items.titel: Environmental DNA is an efficient tool for monitoring pesticide resistance mutations in pest insects
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract BACKGROUND Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding is a revolutionary tool for monitoring biodiversity. In addition, eDNA can also detect the presence and frequency of nuclear genomic mutations in single‐species assays. In agricultural systems, this could provide a powerful tool for detecting and estimating the relative frequency of pesticide resistance mutations in pest arthropods, enabling more targeted resistance management. RESULTS We tested the possibility of using eDNA to detect the presence and frequency of mutations in the voltage‐gated sodium channel (VGSC) conferring pyrethroid resistance in the cabbage‐stem flea beetle (CSFB; Psylliodes chrysocephala ). We first tested the efficiency of eDNA for detecting mutations with a laboratory experiment, in which beetles with known resistance mutations were allowed to interact with cabbage ( Brassica rapa ) leaves. We then tested our approach with two field experiments. First, rapeseed ( Brassica napus ) leaves and individual beetles were collected to compare the relative frequencies of SNPs obtained from eDNA and conventional specimen‐based genotyping. Second, we used previously collected rapeseed stem‐bulk samples from various fields to explore the prevalence of resistance mutations. We show that plant‐derived eDNA can provide insights into the presence and frequency of resistance mutations, which are comparable to single beetle genotyping. items.titel: Achieving Good Quality of Coastal Waters: The Role of Policy Coherence across the Land–Sea Interface
items.samenvatting_bron: Coastal ecosystems are affected by pressures from both land and sea. Ensuring good ecosystem conditions therefore requires ecosystem-based management (EBM) that addresses pressures at their source, regardless of where they originate. The EU Water Framework Directive and Marine Strategy Framework Directive both employ EBM approaches. Yet despite their complementary aims, they fall short of enabling holistic source-to-sea management. Incoherences in scope, scale, and legal force hinder achieving their environmental objectives, while sectoral economic policies often prevail. Case studies from Norway, Finland, and France illustrate varied national responses to these design challenges in EU law. Despite their efforts, none of the cases achieved good coastal water quality. Revisions of EU legislation and policy are needed. Coherence in objectives and measures should be strengthened across the Directives, enabling clearer and better coordinated roles; procedural alignment should reduce duplication and enhance synergies; and stronger legal and financial steering is needed to influence sectoral policies.

items.titel: Cities with birdsong: the impact of forest city designation on bird biodiversity
items.samenvatting_bron: Nature-based solutions such as forest cities are emerging as effective approaches for achieving symbiosis between humans and other species within urban environments. This article centers on China’s National Forest City Designation (NFCD) policy and develops a framework to investigate its impact on biodiversity. This article tests this framework with two key tools: a novel dataset of large-scale birdwatching data from China and a difference-in-differences approach. Research findings reveal that the NFCD policy has spurred a 5.6%−8.0% rise in bird biodiversity, and the regular inspection mechanism guarantees the sustainability of this impact. Increased forest area, improved forest quality, and enhanced forest protection are the primary association mechanisms. Further analysis indicates that NFCD provides greater protection for non-endangered birds, larger-bodied birds, forest-dwelling birds, and resident birds. The NFCD policy yields better results in urban areas as well as regions administered by officials who are younger, better educated, or possess relevant experience. These findings provide novel insights into how tournament-style policies impact urban landscapes and biodiversity.

items.titel: Wetland plant biodiversity in China: a scoping evidence map linking ecosystem services, SDGs, and governance instruments
items.samenvatting_bron: Wetlands are biodiversity hotspots and critical nature-based solutions for water purification, climate regulation, and flood and coastal risk reduction, yet they remain among the world’s most threatened ecosystems. This scoping review synthesized 2,482 China-focused studies published between 2001 and 2026 to examine how wetland plant biodiversity supports ecosystem services and informs governance and United Nations. Multidimensional biodiversity, including taxonomic, compositional, functional, and phylogenetic attributes, was consistently linked to water-quality regulation, carbon sequestration, habitat provision, and flood protection. Major pressures included land conversion, hydrological alteration, pollution, coastal reclamation, invasive species, and climate change. Although few studies explicitly referenced SDGs or named policy instruments, substantial evidence supported SDG 6, 13, 14, and 15. Synthesized within a State–Function–Pressure–Response framework, the findings demonstrate that conserving wetland plant biodiversity is essential for sustaining ecosystem services and strengthening biodiversity-informed wetland governance in China.

items.samenvatting_bron: This workshop was organized to identify strategies for advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) under a changing climate, with a focus on building resilience and promoting sustainable water management in Ethiopia. The workshop format combined academic presentations, group discussions, and a field excursion to a botanic reserve park showcasing successful SDG interventions. A carefully selected group of DAAD Alumni, representing diverse academic disciplines, professional levels (ranging from professors to undergraduates), and geographic regions across the country, convened for a two-day intensive session. Participants drew on their experiences and local realities to deliberate on five thematic areas identified through in-depth literature review and consultations with academic mentors. This study presents an integrated and systematic framework for uncertainty and sensitivity analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of riparian revegetation in reducing downstream flood hazard, demonstrated in the Bundamba Creek sub-catchment, Australia. items.titel: Ecological restoration of the land-sea interface: practices, challenges, and prospects in the Yellow River Delta
items.samenvatting_bron: The ecological degradation of the Yellow River Delta is driven by the coupled effects of multiple land–river–sea stressors, including altered fluvial water and sediment regimes, seawater intrusion, biological invasions, and intensive human activities. However, existing restoration practices remain largely component-specific and therefore have limited capacity to address these interacting pressures. This review synthesizes multidisciplinary evidence to elucidate the major degradation processes, trace the evolution of restoration research, and characterize emerging synergistic restoration practices in the Yellow River Delta. The analysis reveals an increasing research emphasis on ecological connectivity, multi-objective coordination, and system-oriented restoration alongside earlier attention to water–sediment regulation and single-factor restoration. Based on representative practices, we further identify three complementary dimensions of synergistic restoration: elemental synergy, integrating hydrology, salinity, topography, and biological processes; spatial synergy, linking watershed, landscape, estuarine, and nearshore scales; and objective synergy, integrating invasive-species control with native habitat reconstruction. items.titel: A regeneration approach for water and climate sensitive cities in peri-urban zones
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract The rapid expansion of urban areas, along with the increase of impervious surfaces and encroachment on floodplains, has resulted in significant challenges related to flood and climate risk, water quality, biodiversity, and preservation of essential ecosystem services. An effective approach to mitigate these impacts lies in Nature-based Solutions (NbS), which have emerged as promising strategies for enhancing both environmental sustainability and human well-being, and they have been demonstrated to play a pivotal role in climate change adaptation and mitigation. This research aims to quantify the potential effects of NbS on water- and climate-related ecosystem services over a specific site in Legnano city which is a peri-urban zone, western the Milan metropolitan area in the North-West of Italy. The study adopts an integrated approach to urban regeneration, examining how the implementation of NbS can enhance the provision of various ecosystem services. Specifically, pluvial flood storage, heat island mitigation and biodiversity are quantified as primary benefits in the study area. The paper emphasizes the improvement of service indicators through the NbS approach that can be applied to all urban areas, fostering the development of resilient cities and ensuring the well-being of both citizens and ecosystems.

items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Climate change poses disproportionate threats to human health in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), yet comprehensive evidence on implemented interventions remains under-researched. Understanding the scope and characteristics of existing climate-health interventions is essential for informing policy priorities and action in the region. We conducted a scoping review following Arksey and O'Malley's framework and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. We systematically searched Google Scholar, PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus for peer-reviewed empirical studies on climate-health interventions in SSA, with no date restrictions. Two reviewers independently screened 3009 records. A total of 36 studies reporting 350 interventions were included. items.titel: Decoupling hydraulic and treatment optima in floating treatment islands: implications for nature-based solutions in stormwater systems
items.samenvatting_bron: Floating treatment islands (FTIs) are increasingly deployed as nature-based solutions (NbS) in urban stormwater systems. However, conventional design relies on empirical hydraulic proxies, lacking a physics-based framework that integrates multi-scale flow processes with localized reaction kinetics. This study presents a technical increment by quantifying the 3D multi-scale coupling between system-scale hydrodynamics and localized root-zone pollutant uptake using validated computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of a full-scale stormwater pond. The results reveal a clear physical decoupling between hydraulic and treatment optima. Hydraulic efficiency, governed by flow redistribution and short-circuiting mitigation, associated with improved flow distribution and reduced short-circuiting, is maximised at a root-length-to-pond-depth ratio (LR/DP) of approximately 0.50. Conversely, FTI pollutant mass removal – driven by local advective flux and residence time within the porous root matrix – reaches an individual maximum near LR/DP ≈ 0.65, with the upstream island achieving 52% removal. Crucially, system-scale pollutant removal plateaus beyond LR/DP = 0.50 (62% at both 0.50 and 0.65), as flow blockage by deep upstream roots induces hydraulic shielding over downstream structures. Consequently, LR/DP ≈ 0.50 represents a robust, physics-informed design optimum, maximizing water quality benefits while preserving hydraulic performance, structural stability, and cost-efficiency.

items.titel: Transformações no uso e cobertura da terra e seus reflexos socioambientais em uma bacia hidrográfica periurbana de Campo Grande – Mato Grosso do Sul
items.samenvatting_bron: Disordered urbanization, characterized by excessive soil sealing, inadequate structural interventions, and effluent discharge, results in severe water degradation, a scenario historically observed in Campo Grande − Mato Grosso do Sul. In this context, this study analyzed the socio-environmental impacts of urbanization and macro-drainage works in a peri-urban watershed in the northern zone of the city. The methodology integrated the analysis of geotechnical maps, cartographic materials, the MapBiomas historical series (1985–2024), and fieldwork. The results demonstrated a drastic alteration in the landscape: the urbanized area jumped from 12.70% in 1985 to 42.72% in 2024, reducing native vegetation to only 13.06%. Rapid urban growth on fragile soils (Entisols - Quartzipsamments), combined with unfinished interventions, intensified erosive processes and generated high socio-environmental costs. Macro-drainage works received millions in public investments but failed to mitigate the impacts. In the Cônsul Assaf Trad Park, a stalled construction project left an environmental liability characterized by active erosion, silted reservoirs, and a dam rupture in 2019. Obstruction of the riverbed by construction waste and clandestine sewage connections was also observed. It is concluded that the lack of urban planning exacerbated the environmental fragility of the watershed, making the adoption of Nature-based Solutions imperative for the recovery and ecological restoration of the area.

Over de HSL, gelegen tussen Hoofddorp en de Belgische grens, rijden zo’n 300 treinen per dag. Het is de enige hogesnelheidslijn in Nederland ontworpen om met 300 kilometer per uur over te rijden. Treinen kunnen echter momenteel over een deel van het traject maar tot 120 kilometer per uur rijden vanwege problemen met de infrastructuur. De lijn is opgeleverd in 2006 en sindsdien is Infraspeed verantwoordelijk voor het beheer en onderhoud van de HSL. Per 1 april 2031 neemt ProRail deze taken over. De HSL staat de komende jaren voor vier samenhangende opgaven die bepalend zijn voor een betrouwbare en toekomstbestendige hogesnel- heidsverbinding. document.tekst_begin: Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal 2 Vergaderjaar 2025–2026 Aanhangsel van de Handelingen Vragen gesteld door de leden der Kamer, met de daarop door de regering gegeven antwoorden 2985 Vragen van het lid Coenradie (JA21) aan de Minister van Justitie en Veiligheid over het Centrum Seksueel Geweld als toegangspoort voor zedenzaken (ingezonden 19 juni 2026). Antwoord van Minister Van Weel (Justitie en Veiligheid), mede namens de Staatssecretaris van Justitie en Veiligheid en de Minister van Langdurige Zorg, Jeugd en Sport (ontvangen 8 september 2026). Zie ook Aanhangsel Handelingen, vergaderjaar 2025–2026, nr. 2535. items.titel: Spatio-Temporal Dynamics of Urban Heat Islands and Sustainable Urban Development in a Rapidly Urbanizing Tropical City
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Rapid urbanization in tropical cities is intensifying surface urban heat island (SUHI) effects, posing significant challenges for sustainable urban planning. Hence, the present study investigates the spatio-temporal dynamics of land surface temperature (LST) and its relationship with vegetation and built-up indices in Raipur district, India, between 2015 and 2025. The multi-temporal Landsat imagery processed on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) was used to derive normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), normalized difference built-up index (NDBI), and LST, followed by SUHI intensity assessment and correlation analysis. The results reveal a clear spatial pattern in which urban and peri-urban areas exhibit elevated LST values, while vegetated rural zones act as thermal buffers. The NDVI-LST showed a consistent negative correlation (− 0.51 to − 0.33), highlighting the cooling role of vegetation, whereas LST-NDBI showed a consistent strong positive correlation (0.76–0.82), highlighting the warming impact of impervious surfaces. Change detection analysis indicates declining vegetation cover in peri-urban zones and expansion of built-up areas, contributing to outward propagation of thermal hotspots. Although SUHI intensity showed a relative decline over time, this was primarily driven by rising rural temperatures rather than urban cooling, suggesting regional thermal homogenization. items.titel: WILDLIFE UNDERPASSES AS INTEGRATED CIVIL AND ECOLOGICAL INFRASTRUCTURE: A Conceptual Design Framework for Highway Connectivity
items.samenvatting_bron: This report, titled “Wildlife Underpasses as Integrated Civil and Ecological Infrastructure: A Conceptual Design Framework for Highway Connectivity,” examines the integration of civil engineering principles and ecological considerations in the conceptual planning of wildlife underpasses along highways. The report discusses wildlife–vehicle collisions, habitat fragmentation, wildlife-crossing infrastructure, underpass planning and design considerations, drainage and hydraulic requirements, structural and geotechnical considerations, construction practices, maintenance, monitoring, and environmental management. It presents a conceptual framework intended to support safer wildlife movement and improved ecological connectivity across transportation infrastructure. The report is based on a review of relevant literature and published guidance. It is a conceptual technical study and does not claim original field surveys, site-specific investigations, or experimentally validated structural designs. Actual implementation would require site-specific ecological assessments, geotechnical investigations, hydraulic analysis, structural design, and approval by the relevant authorities. Institutional affiliation: Dr. D. Y. Patil Polytechnic, Kasaba Bawada, Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India.

items.titel: Evaluating environmental DNA metabarcoding for describing freshwater fish and shellfish occurrence in an Eastern Cascades watershed
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Objective Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding offers a promising, cost-effective tool to collect data across a large spatial scale, but analyzing these data poses several critical decisions that are uncommon to traditional field sampling. The objective of our study was to evaluate data collection, filtering, and analytical components of occurrence data generated using an eDNA metabarcoding approach. Methods During 2024, we collected replicated water samples from 89 sites distributed across the Wenatchee River Hydrologic Unit Code 8 watershed located in eastern Washington. We processed samples using two metabarcoding markers that targeted the cytochrome c oxidase subunit 1 (CO1; Leray-XT) or 12S ribosomal RNA (MiFish-U) mitochondrial gene region, and we summarized differences in detection, taxonomic coverage, and data filtering requirements for each marker. Finalized metabarcoding data were used to fit occupancy models within a Bayesian framework. We evaluated model results with a focus on species-specific detection probability, the stability of predictions using the full data set and reduced numbers of visited sites, and comparisons between fitting models using a single-species or multispecies occupancy model approach. Results The metabarcoding approach generated detections for 26 unique taxonomic assignment groups that closely matched species-level assignments for fish and shellfish. items.titel: An Open-Source Design Intervention Support Tool for Climate Resilience: Guiding Agroforestry in the Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystems (WEFE) Nexus Systems
items.samenvatting_bron: The TRANS-SAHARA project supports climate change adaptation and mitigation in the Greater Northern African Region through scalable agroforestry systems embedded in a Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystems (WEFE) Nexus framework. This approach recognizes the interdependence of resources and promotes integrated, sustainable solutions in vulnerable contexts. The main objective of this research is to design and develop a decision-making support tool assisting researchers, policymakers, and local stakeholders in planning agroforestry interventions across regional Living Labs, local community-based sites where innovations are co-created and tested with project stakeholders. The tool aims to enable comprehensive analysis by integrating environmental, hydrological, socio-economic, and governance-related data, facilitating an inclusive evaluation of trade-offs and synergies. By incorporating multi-stakeholder perspectives, it supports more holistic and robust decision-making—an essential feature given the inherently multi-factor nature of the optimization problem the project aims to address. Effective collaboration and impact in sustainability research hinge on the open sharing of data and metadata. The tool is built upon Eurac’s research data infrastructure, known as the Environmental Data Platform (EDP). We performed a feasibility study in mice comparing IV tail-vein injection with intratracheal microspray instillation of the clinical agent iohexol. Mice received iohexol (100 µL, 500 mg/mL) by either route. Whole-body projections were acquired to 120 min and thoracic sections to 30 min, each animal scanned before contrast in the same session. Contrast distribution was recorded by compartment and quantified from regions of interest. items.titel: Ag/Ti Electrodes for Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction: Revealing Highly Effective Interfaces by In‐Situ Electrochemical Mass Spectrometry
items.samenvatting_bron: The electrochemical reduction of nitrate to hydroxyl amine or ammonia is a prominent means to effectively valorize agricultural effluent emissions. We demonstrate that bimetallic electrodes, composed of Ag nanoparticles deposited on Ti metal, exhibit a pronounced synergy in nitrate reduction in acidic electrolyte. This is evidenced by in‐situ electrochemical mass spectrometry (EC‐MS), showing NO evolution in a complex potential‐dependent profile at lower onset potentials compared to single metal Ag or Ti electrodes. Furthermore, liquid phase analysis shows a significant Faradaic efficiency to hydroxylamine for Ag/Ti electrodes, even at potentials above 0 V RHE , i.e., requiring at least a 200–300 mV lower overpotential than necessary for the single metal electrodes. We discuss favorable NO and hydroxylamine formation to be occurring on highly effective Ag/Ti interfaces. This work highlights the importance of interfaces and suggests that optimization of (Ag/Ti) bimetallic electrodes appears to be a valuable means to develop high performance electrodes for the reduction of nitrate in acidic conditions.

items.titel: Multiscenario Simulation and Prediction of Urban Green Space in the Changle District of Fuzhou City, China, Based on Multiobjective Optimization and a GeoSOS-FLUS Model
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Green spaces in densely urbanized areas along China’s southeast coast generally face spatial competition between ecological protection and development intensity, as well as conflicts between policy-oriented and market-driven values. Among them, Changle District in Fuzhou City, as the core area of the coastal new city, needs to coordinate its green space system to address complex three-dimensional problems. To explore the optimal configuration of green spaces under different ecological constraints and achieve a balance between ecological, economic, and social benefits, this paper takes Changle District in Fuzhou City as the research area, with 2020 as the base year, and innovatively combines a multiobjective optimization model with the Geographic Simulation and Optimization System–Future Land Use Simulation (GeoSOS-FLUS) model. The former is used to balance multiple objectives such as ecological conservation, economic development, and social needs, generating optimal allocation schemes. The latter precisely simulates the dynamic evolution of green spaces based on these schemes. Together, they overcome the limitations of traditional models, which cannot account for economic and ecological benefits when simulating complex urban land use. Based on this model combination, this paper simulates and predicts the area structure, spatial configuration, and target benefits of green space in Changle District in 2030 under ecological high-, medium-, and low-constraint scenarios.

items.titel: Evidence for potential top-down control of meso- and micro-copepods during jellyfish blooms revealed by eDNA metabarcoding
items.samenvatting_bron: The limitation of traditional survey methods has catalyzed the rapid development and widespread application of eDNA metabarcoding. The results indicate that Aurelia coerulea is predominantly distributed in the northern Laizhou Bay, while Nemopilema nomurai is mainly found in the transition zone of Bohai and Yellow Seas. This distribution pattern may be attributed to different habitat selectivity during the polyp stage as well as environmental adaptability and ocean current effect during the medusa stage. The relative read abundance (RRA) of A. coerulea was significantly negatively correlated with that of meso- and micro-copepods, a pattern consistent with a potential top-down effect; however, under potentially phosphorus-limiting conditions, this inverse association did not cascade into an increase in phytoplankton biomass reflected by Chl a variation. Instead, elevated jellyfish RRA was associated with increased water turbidity. Our study provides a methodological paradigm for applying eDNA approach to elucidate the ecological consequences of regional jellyfish blooms, with future potential for scaling up to ecosystem-level investigations.

Climate change, population growth, land-use alteration, urbanization, and increasing water demand have intensified drought frequency, duration, and severity in many regions, creating unprecedented pressure on water resource systems. This chapter examines the interrelationship between drought management and water resources through a comprehensive analysis of drought concepts, classifications, drivers, impacts, assessment methods, monitoring systems, mitigation strategies, policy frameworks, and adaptive management approaches. The chapter discusses meteorological, hydrological, agricultural, and socio-economic droughts and evaluates major drought indices, including SPI, SPEI, PDSI, and remote sensing-based indicators. Particular attention is given to Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM), groundwater sustainability, reservoir operation, drought preparedness planning, climate adaptation, and nature-based solutions (NbS). items.titel: Policy Frameworks for Managing Water Resources
items.samenvatting_bron: This chapter examines the design of policy frameworks for managing water resources under the increasing pressure of natural hazards, including floods, droughts, wildfires, and cascading climate-related risks. Moving beyond traditional reactive crisis management, the chapter argues for a shift toward integrated, risk-informed governance that embeds resilience into the routine functions of water policy, planning, and investment. It explores how legal foundations, institutional coordination, economic instruments, and technical monitoring systems can be harmonized to manage water security amidst deep uncertainty. The chapter emphasizes that resilience is not achieved solely through engineered infrastructure; it requires a diversified approach that integrates the nature-based solutions, land-use management, social protection, and inclusive governance. By highlighting the necessity of adaptive planning, transparent data governance, and equity-focused decision-making, the chapter provides a conceptual and practical guide for developing policy environments capable of sustaining water services and protecting communities, ecosystems, and economies against recurring and compounding natural threats.

It argues that floods, droughts, landslides, storm surges, and water quality crises should not be understood as purely natural events, but as socio-hydrological risks shaped by land use, infrastructure design, governance quality, and the interaction between human and ecological systems. Within this perspective, IWRM offers a practical basis for reducing disaster risk by integrating water, land, ecosystems, and institutions at the basin scale. The chapter explores how IWRM contributes to mitigation through coordinated flood and drought management, watershed protection, groundwater regulation, ecosystem restoration, pollution control, and adaptive governance. items.samenvatting_bron: Flood risk has become one of the most significant global environmental and socio-economic challenges due to rapid urbanization, climate change, land-use transformation, and increasing pressure on water resources. Simultaneously, water resource dynamics are undergoing substantial changes driven by alterations in precipitation regimes, river discharge variability, groundwater depletion, snowmelt processes, and extreme hydrological events. This chapter examines the complex relationship between flood risk and water resource dynamics by exploring the hydrological, climatic, environmental, and socio-economic factors that influence flood occurrence and severity. items.titel: Natural Hazard Implications
items.samenvatting_bron: This chapter examines the profound implications of intensifying natural hazards for the future of global water resources management. As anthropogenic climate change, rapid urbanization, and land-use shifts converge, the traditional reliance on historical hydrologic data as a guide for future design, the paradigm of stationarity, is increasingly untenable. This transition necessitates a shift toward a management philosophy defined by deep uncertainty, systemic resilience, and adaptive governance. The analysis first characterizes the complex interactions between hydrometeorological and geophysical hazards, such as floods, droughts, wildfire-induced watershed degradation, and sea-level rise, emphasizing their tendency to compound and cascade across human and natural systems. It subsequently explores the technical and institutional vulnerabilities inherent in current water infrastructure, agricultural water use, and urban supply systems. A critical focus is placed on emerging frameworks for resilience, including the integration of nature-based solutions, adaptive policy pathways, and digital innovations like real-time monitoring and digital twinning. document.tekst_begin: Een Onmenselijke Wet – o n d e r z o e k s r a p p o r t O p 27 november 2021 maakte het Nederlandse kabinet publieke excuses voor het leed dat transgender en intersekse personen is aangedaan onder de voormalige wet op de wijziging van geslachtsregistratie (1985-2014). Dit rapport komt voort uit een opdracht van het Ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap (ocw), directie Emancipatie en is onafhankelijk uitgevoerd door onder- zoekers van de Radboud Universiteit, verbonden aan het Radboud Institute for Culture & History (rich). In deze rapportage worden ervaringen van transgender en intersekse personen onderzocht die schade en leed hebben ondervonden door de invoering en toepassing van de voor - m alige wet en de voorwaarden die daarbij hoorden. Het doel van de onderzoeksopdracht is zo bij te dragen aan bredere maatschappelijke erkenning en grotere bekendheid in de maatschappij van de gevolgen van de wet voor de mensen die hierdoor getroffen zijn. De titel van het rapport ‘Een onmenselijke wet’ verwijst naar de mensenrechten die geschonden werden door de voorwaarden verbonden aan de wet en waarvoor namens de Staat excuses zijn gemaakt. Het prioriteringskader voor transportverzoeken is opgesteld door de toezichthouder de Autoriteit Consument en Markt (ACM). De ACM heeft de exclusieve bevoegdheid om regels en voorwaarden op te stellen voor het verkrijgen van toegang tot het elektriciteitsnet. Daarbinnen passen ook de regels over voorrang. Sinds 1 oktober 2024 zijn netbeheerders verplicht het prioriteringskader van de ACM toe te passen. Sinds 1 januari 2026 geldt een vernieuwd prioriteringskader. Dat was nodig na een rechterlijke uitspraak van het College van Beroep voor het bedrijfsleven (CBb). Sinds 1 juli 2026 wordt het prioriteringskader ook toegepast voor kleinverbruiksaansluitingen. Voorheen reserveerden netbeheerders transportcapaciteit voor kleinverbruikers, maar deze werkwijze deed geen recht aan het prioriteringskader en was daarom niet langer houdbaar. items.samenvatting_bron: None. Zaak:

document.tekst_begin: Reserves in het funderend onderwijs Financiële factoren die samenhangen met de reserves Juli 2026 Geld dat voor onderwijs bestemd is, moet aan onderwijs uitgegeven worden en niet onnodig in reserves zitten. Tegelijkertijd is het ook belangrijk dat besturen ervoor zorgen dat zij genoeg reserves hebben om in de toekomst aan hun verplichtingen te voldoen. Om beter te begrijpen welke financiële factoren samenhangen met de hoogte van de reserves, onderzocht de inspectie de financiële gegevens van alle schoolbesturen in het funderend onderwijs over de periode 2018- 2024. [Voorwoord:] De financiële reserves van besturen vragen al jaren de aandacht. Middelen die bedoeld zijn voor goed onderwijs, blijven soms onnodig lang op de plank liggen. Juist daarom is doordacht reservebeheer belangrijk. In dit onderzoek zien we dat besturen met veel vaste activa en een hogere rijksbekostiging gemiddeld ook hogere reserves hebben. Ook zien we dat besturen die relatief meer investeren in personeel juist lagere reserves aanhouden. Er is geen vaste norm voor de juiste hoogte van een reserve. Tegelijkertijd is huidkanker in belangrijke mate te voorkomen. Overmatige blootstelling aan uv-straling is de belangrijkste vermijdbare risicofactor. Adequate zonbescherming verkleint het risico op huidkanker. Juist nu de noodzaak van effectieve preventie groeit, kan medische desinformatie over zonbescherming deze preventie ondermijnen. Het is essentieel dat mensen beschikken over betrouwbare informatie en weten hoe zij zichzelf kunnen beschermen. 2. document.tekst_begin: In een samenleving waarin informatie zich sneller verspreidt dan een besmettelijk virus en iedereen via online platforms een groot publiek kan bereiken, neemt het belang van betrouwbare (gezondheids)informatie toe. Medische misinformatie en desinformatie kunnen het vertrouwen in gezondheidsadviezen en publieke gezondheidsmaatregelen onder druk zetten en daadwerkelijke gezondheidsschade veroorzaken. Daarom is een betrouwbare informatievoorziening een essentiële randvoorwaarde voor een goede publieke gezondheid. GGD’en hebben hierin een belangrijke rol door vragen, zorgen en misverstanden dicht bij inwoners te signaleren en betrouwbare informatie toegankelijk te maken via lokale netwerken en persoonlijk contact. Medische desinformatie vraagt om betrouwbare informatie én vertrouwen dichtbij Goede publieke gezondheid begint bij mensen die betrouwbare informatie weten te vinden, begrijpen en erop kunnen vertrouwen. Vooral wanneer betrouwbare informatie ontbreekt of niet goed vindbaar is, kunnen onjuiste of misleidende berichten zich snel verspreiden. De CSDDD is een Europese richtlijn die ervoor moet zorgen dat grote ondernemingen die actief zijn op de Europese interne markt nadelige gevolgen op de mensenrechten en het milieu in hun waardeketens zoveel mogelijk voorkomen. De Omnibus I is op 18 maart 2026 officieel in werking getreden en moet voor 1 juli 2028 worden geïmplementeerd in nationale wetgeving. De Europese Commissie heeft van 12 juni 2026 tot 24 juli 2026 een openbare raadpleging uitgezet voor de richtsnoeren die worden ontwikkeld ter ondersteuning van de CSDDD. Afgelopen jaar hebben we overal in Nederland weer laten zien hoe Sanquin vormgeeft aan haar belangrijke taak, de Nederlandse bloedvoorziening: met betrokkenheid, deskundigheid, verantwoordelijkheid en samenwerk ing. Ook onder lastige omstandigheden – van winterse logistiek tot piekmomenten op onze locaties – hielden we de bloedvoorziening op peil. Dat kon alleen dankzij de betrokkenheid van onze donors en de inzet van onze collega’s. Samen zorgen we, elke dag, voor veilige en hoogwaardige bloedproducten voor patiënten in heel Nederland. Een donorcommunity die gezond en trouw is, maximale toegevoegde waarde van onze producten en diensten aan de samenleving en een bedrijfsvoering die op orde is. document.tekst_begin: Goedemiddag, Het lid Bolhuis (PRO)zou graag een rondetafelgesprek voeren over ‘Efficiënt Armoedebeleid’ te houden voor de begrotingsbehandeling SZW begin december. Dit willen we dinsdag bij de procedurevergadering aanvragen. Op dit moment hadden we bedacht om twee rondes te doen, de eerste ronde met maatschappelijke organisaties en de tweede ronde met een meer wetenschappelijke invalshoek. Voor de tweede ronde denken we nu aan Nibud, Commissie Sociaal Minimum, Ecorys (over hun onderzoek ‘Kwetsbare gezinnen in maatschappelijk perspectief’) en Monitor Utrecht. Met een aantal van deze organisaties hebben we hier contact over gehad. Uiteraard zal er een voorbereidingsgroep komen maar dan weten jullie alvast wat onze insteek is.

Annemiek Harder, Erasmus Universiteit Rotterdam Kindermishandeling in de jeugdhulp Niet alleen thuis, maar ook in de jeugdhulp - waar jongeren terechtkomen als hun situatie thuis problematisch is - komt kindermishandeling voor. Sterker nog, er zijn in de afgelopen decennia diverse onderzoeken in Nederland en het buitenland uitgevoerd waaruit blijkt dat kindermishandeling in de jeugdhulp relatief vaak voorkomt1-7. De kans op mishandeling is voor jongeren in de jeugdhulp bijna drie keer zo groot als voor jongeren die thuis wonen8. Daarom is het cruciaal om alert te zijn op kindermishandeling in de jeugdhulp, dit actief te voorkomen en direct in te grijpen als het toch misgaat. 1. document.tekst_begin: 1 Inbreng Filomena over kindermishandeling Het kind zien en blijven luisteren Rondetafelgesprek Tweede Kamer 28 oktober 2026 | 20 oktober 2026 Kinderen die ernstig geweld meemaken, hebben recht op bescherming en passende hulp. Ook kinderen die getuige zijn van psychisch of fysiek geweld tegen een ouder, zijn slachtoffer. Bij Filomena geven we hen een eigen plek, brengen we deskundigheid samen en blijven we betrokken zolang dat nodig is voor duurzame veiligheid. Wij vragen de Tweede Kamer de voorwaarden te organiseren om deze aanpak landelijk mogelijk te maken. Wat kinderen nu in de weg zit (medische)Zorg, jeugdbescherming, politie en justitie werken met verschillende toegangsroutes, taken en besluitmomenten. Informatie blijft versnipperd en expertise rond bijvoorbeeld huiselijk geweld ontbreekt. document.tekst_begin: 1 Samenvattende inleiding In dit position paper geven wij een reflectie op de positie van mishandelde kinderen in wet- en regelgeving en de onderliggende uitwerking hiervan in handelingsprotocollen. Een goede meld-, advies- en onderzoeksfunctie vormt het hart in een beschermingsstelsel dat reikt van preventie kindermishandeling tot passende hulpverlening. De Rijksoverheid draagt conform het Kinderrechtenverdrag de stelselverantwoordelijkheid hiervoor. Maar Veilig Thuis luidde vorige week de noodklok: het aantal meldingen stijgt, de complexiteit neemt toe en er is onvoldoende lokale en regionale hulp beschikbaar waarnaar verwezen kan worden. Met als gevolg dat ouders en kinderen in risicovolle onveiligheidssituaties op wachtlijsten staan, burgers en professionals aarzelen contact op te nemen en de kwaliteit van geleverde diensten afneemt. Dit is geen verrassing, maar een ontwikkeling die al jarenlang gaande is, ook bij Gecertificeerde Instellingen. De huidige situatie vraagt daarom én om voldoende capaciteit voor het werk dat vandaag moet gebeuren, én om een fundamentele bezinning op het gehele stelsel voor kinderen met ernstige signalen van mishandeling. document.tekst_begin: Ontwikkelingen in Tabaksspeciaalzaken Mei 2026 Deze factsheet beschrijft ontwikkelingen binnen de uitgezonderde speciaalzaken als specifiek verkoopkanaal van rookwaren. Het gaat om een casus waarbij een tabaksfabrikant de inrichting van verschillende speciaalzaken regelt. En om een monitor naar en signalen over de aanwezige reclame en commerciële ontwikkelingen in speciaalzaken. De speciaalzaak is een bijzonder type verkooppunt. Speciaalzaken zijn onder voorwaarden uitgezonderd van het uitstalverbod en reclameverbod voor rookwaren. Zij mogen de producten nog tonen en bepaalde reclame voor rookwaren maken. In dat geval moeten zij geregistreerd zijn bij de NVWA. Er zijn twee typen speciaalzaken, speciaalzaken (categorie lid 1 van artikel 5.9 uit het Tabaks-en rookwarenbesluit) die uitsluitend tabaksproducten, aanverwante producten (en daarbij behorende accessoires), deelnamebewijzen aan kansspelen en dagbladen verkopen en speciaalzaken (categorie lid 2 van artikel 5.9 uit het Tabaks- en rookwarenbesluit) met een jaaromzet van maximaal 900.000 euro waarvan minimaal 75 procent behaald is uit rookwaren. Van dit tweede type speciaalzaken kunnen zich geen nieuwe bedrijven meer aanmelden

items.titel: Valorisation of PET-rich mixed plastic waste using a cascading concept involving selective ammonolysis and catalytic pyrolysis
items.samenvatting_bron: We report a cascading valorisation strategy for real polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-rich waste streams, combining selective ammonolysis of PET with catalytic pyrolysis of the non-PET residue. In this approach, PET-rich packaging waste is treated with ammonia in ethylene glycol to produce terephthaldiamide (TDA), while the remaining polyolefin (PO)-rich residue is subsequently upgraded to benzene, toluene, xylene (BTX), and light olefins over H-ZSM-5 catalyst. TDA is a valuable aromatic diamide and a potential precursor to p -phenylene diamine, a monomer used in the production of poly(p-phenyleneterephthalamide) (PPTA). For post-consumer PET trays, ammonolysis at 5 bar NH 3 , and 100 °C for 8 h, followed by a downstream separation procedure, resulted in an almost quantitative conversion of PET, yielding pure TDA as small crystals in 74 wt% (87 mol%) yield based on the PET content in the feed. The residue (mostly polyolefins) was converted to BTX (5 wt% on residue), and propene/butenes (19 wt%, on residue) using a catalytic in situ pyrolysis approach with H-ZSM-5 at 550 °C. The same strategy was applied to a PET-enriched, DKR-350 mixed-plastic packaging fraction, affording TDA in 71 wt% (87 mol%) yield based on the PET content, while catalytic pyrolysis of the residue produced BTX (3 wt%) and propene/isobutene (4 wt%) based on the residue. items.titel: Climate-Based Modeling of Invasive Species Impact on Urban Green Infrastructure Using CLIMEX and Remote Sensing Data
items.samenvatting_bron: The pace at which invasive alien species are established and spread is becoming a threat, especially to urban ecosystems, due, in part, to the variability of climates, urban growth, and fragmentation of habitats. These biological invasions are highly dangerous to urban green infrastructure (UGI), which sabotages biodiversity, ecological services, and ecological resilience in the long term. A unravelled modelling approach to employ the CLIMEX model of species distribution as well as the spatial analysis of ecosystems via remote sensing to observe invasion risk zones and map them in the fast urbanising landscapes was created in this work. The climatic suitability of chosen invasive species in the current and future climate conditions under parameters serving as temperature, precipitation, and humidity was simulated with the help of the CLIMEX model, and the land cover dynamics and vegetation indices (as well as the urban heat islands) were measured with the assistance of remote sensing data (Sentinel-2 and ModiS) measurements. It was possible to integrate these datasets using a GIS based multi-criteria methodology to create an Invasion Risk Index (IRI) to predict ecologically sensitive regions. The findings indicated that areas with an average rainfall, increasing temperatures, and discontinuous vegetation shows high ecological suitability of the invasive species, and this would be more so at the urban fringes, transport corridors, and industrial areas. items.titel: Role of Urban Forestry in Future Sustainability from an African Perspective
items.samenvatting_bron: The size of urban land is constantly increasing following the augmentation of the urban population and urbanization practices, which affect the management of urban green spaces. In addition to that, the manifestations of climate change such as droughts, floods and increased temperature are expected to further degrade urban and peri-urban forests. Urban and peri-urban forests degradation undermine the vast array of ecosystem services on which the urbanites rely on. This chapter highlights the role of urban forestry in promoting urban sustainability and management of challenges such as urban tree mortality in Africa, with special reference to Niger. The chapter also describes the history of urban forestry, urban forest types such as forgotten urban forests and urban mosque forests. Moreover, the chapter points out the role of women in creating urban green spaces in dryland cities like Niamey. The drivers of urban forest depletion are presented with special reference to Niger, West African Sahel. The chapter recommends the extensive use of multipurpose tree species in urban tree plantation initiative in the large-scale urban mosques. The chapter also recommends incorporating urban mosque forests in urban planning, climate change policy related to urban tree planting initiatives for urban biodiversity conservation and combating the effects of climate change in cities in Niger.
